results.title: 征信花了还有什么办法可以办理银行贷款? - 知乎
results.summary: 征信花了的情况下,要想办理银行贷款,那得看题主的资质是否够硬,才有线下沟通的可能。 一般走线下银行贷款的准入门槛是:银行白名单客户或者高资产人群, 其中白名单客户一般是: 1、公务员事业单位、国央企、上市公司、500强员工以及少数高精特新单位员工,才有资格进入银行的白名单,才有机会申请银行的线下贷款; 2、高资产人群:名下有存款或者房产余值高,那可以尝试做农商、村镇银行的线下贷款。 3、对银行贡献度高,如一些存款大户单位的财务经理或者负责人,也是可以走线下特批。 总之:贷款征信花只能做线下产品,而线下产品需要资质好,人工沟通能力强。
results.snippet: 一般走线下银行贷款的准入门槛是:银行白名单客户或者高资产人群 ... 名下有存款或者房产余值高,那可以尝试做农商、村镇银行的线下贷款。 3 ... 贷款征信花只能做线下产品,而线下产品需要资质好,人工沟通能力强。

results.title: 征信花了还能借到钱吗? - 知乎
results.summary: 一、先分清:你是哪种“征信花” 1. 轻度花(只查询多,无逾期) 近3个月硬查询(贷款/信用卡审批)6次以上、网贷申请多,但无任何逾期、无当前欠款逾期、负债可控。 ✅ 有机会借钱,但纯信用贷通过率大幅下降。 2. 中度花(查询多+少量短期逾期) 有1-2次1-30天逾期,已结清,当前无逾期。 ✅ 银行信用贷基本拒,抵押/担保、持牌消费金融还有机会。 3. 重度花(查询爆炸+多次逾期/当前逾期/呆账) 连续逾期、当前还有欠款没还、多头网贷高负债。 ❌ 绝大多数正规渠道直接拒,只能走高成本抵押,无抵押基本借不到。 二、能借到钱的正规渠道(按靠谱、低成本排序) 1. 抵押/质押贷款(通过率最高) 名下有房产、全款车、寿险保单、定期存款、理财,去银行/持牌机构办抵押贷。 - 优势:对征信容忍度最高,哪怕征信很花也能批;额度高、利率相对可控 - 缺点:需要资产,流程慢,逾期会没收抵押物 2. 线下城商行、农商行小额信贷 国有大行对查询极严,但地方小银行风控宽松,看重本地工作、公积金、流水。 适合:有稳定社保/公积金、无当前逾期,只是查询多。 3. 持牌消费金融(线上正规网贷) 马上、招联、360借条等持牌机构,比银行宽松,但利率更高(年化10%-24%)。 ⚠️ 缺点:再申请会新增查询,越点越花,容易以贷养贷。 4. 担保贷款 找征信干净、有稳定收入的亲友做担保人,部分银行可放宽征信要求。 5. 已有信用卡备用金/分期 手里现有信用卡的e招贷、现金分期,多数不新增大额硬查询,优先用这个应急。 三、绝对不能碰的坑(号称“无视征信、黑白户可下”) 1. 无牌照私贷、线下高利贷:年化远超法定上限,暴力催收、砍头息、高额违约金。 2. 网贷中介、内部通道:收高额服务费,大概率造假流水骗贷,涉嫌违法,钱没借到先亏钱。 3. 套路贷:虚假合同、强行续贷,债务越滚越大。 4. 所谓“征信修复、洗白征信”:全是骗局,征信只能靠时间养好,无法人为删除正常记录。 四、征信花了借钱的致命误区 1. 一家拒了疯狂换平台点 每申请一次新增1条硬查询,机构判定你极度缺钱,后续全部秒拒,越点越难借。 2. 借新网贷还旧贷(以贷养贷) 负债持续升高,征信彻底废掉,最后所有平台全部封停。 五、低成本解决思路(优先推荐,比借钱更重要) 1. 强制停申3–6个月 不再点任何贷款、测额度、办信用卡,不再新增硬查询,征信会慢慢“干净”。 2. 降低负债 结清小额网贷,信用卡使用率控制在30%以内,减少多头授信。 3. 按时还款养记录 现有信用卡、贷款绝不逾期,连续6–12个月良好记录,审批通过率明显回升。 4. 短期应急优先:信用卡分期 > 抵押贷 > 持牌消费金融,坚决远离私贷。 总结 - 只查询多、无逾期:有正规渠道可借,但优先养征信; - 有逾期、高负债:纯信用贷基本借不到,只能抵押/担保; - 当前还有逾期没结清:绝大多数正规机构直接拒; - 无论多急用钱,不要碰无牌照私贷、中介洗白,只会加重债务危机。

results.title: 征信花,负债高,综合评分不足去哪里贷?还能贷到款吗?
results.summary:
# 征信花,负债高,综合评分不足去哪里贷?还能贷到款吗?

钱云2025-09-01 16:56

1288

征信有点花、负债不低，申请贷款总被拒，说“综合评分不足”——这可能是不少朋友最近遇到的头疼事。别慌，这类情况其实也有办法，不少机构仍然有适配的产品，关键是找对方向、用对方法。

一、哪些渠道还能尝试?

银行常规信贷通道通常对征信和负债要求较高，被拒属于正常。但部分银行也有针对非标客群的产品，比如某些城商行或农商行的“消费贷”或“小微助力贷”，它们往往更看重本地收入稳定性而不是纯粹的征信分数。不妨带上工资流水、社保记录等材料，去线下网点找信贷经理聊一聊。

一些持牌消费金融公司也是可选范围，它们对负债的容忍度相对高一些，审批流程也比银行更灵活。虽然利率可能略高一点，但作为临时周转还是能派上用场。只是要注意，尽量选择持牌机构，避开那些不靠谱的网贷平台。

如果你有房产或车辆，不妨考虑抵押类贷款。这类产品因为有了抵押物，风控逻辑不一样，对征信和负债的要求会大幅放宽。哪怕征信有点问题，只要资产清晰、有还款来源，也有机会获批。

二、如何提高通过率?

不管选择哪种方式，尽量把材料准备齐全。工资流水、社保公积金缴纳记录、房产证明、营业执照(如果是小微业主)等，都能帮你增强信用背书。系统看的是分数，但人审看的是你的整体稳定性。

同时，建议短期内不要再频繁申请贷款。每申请一次，机构就会查一次征信，查询次数太多反而会让征信“更花”，陷入恶性循环。稳住节奏，做好准备再尝试。

三、要不要找助贷服务?

如果自己搞不定，也可以考虑找正规助贷平台帮忙。他们对各家的风控政策更熟悉，可以帮你匹配更适合的产品，甚至提前预审材料、提出优化建议。不过一定要找有资质、收费透明的机构，避免被额外收取高额服务费。

总之，征信花负债高不代表完全没出路，只是需要调整策略、找准渠道。尽量优先选择银行类产品或持牌机构，谨慎使用非银行融资工具，同时稳住征信不再恶化。

以上是关于征信花负债高如何贷款的介绍，如果还有不清楚的，可以咨询在线客服，让信贷顾问一对一帮你解答困惑、匹配方案。

如果征信花了,认真阅读下面文章,可以解决大部分问题。 不讲案例,只教方法 (方法都是历经大量案例总结) 第一步,先确定自己征信有没有花 1.贷款机构查询多 贷款审批,信用卡审批,担保资格审查,资信审查,保前审查等带审字的查询,都属于硬查询(个别银行只计算贷款审批+信用卡审批,个别银行只计算贷款审批,有些银行法人企业查询也不计算在内),一个月超过3次,三个月超过8次,半年超过15次,近一年非银查询过多(非银查询是指查询机构不包含银行两个字的查询),近三个月或者近半年有集中查询(近三天连续查询超过3次以上属于集中查询,如果申请贷款连续三次拒绝,就缓一缓等一两个月再申请),贷后管理不算查询次数。 本人查询(软查询)近一个月最好也不要超过两次。 最安全的周期计算方法,31天为一个月统计周期,倒推31天算近一个月,倒推62天算近二个月,以此类推。如果不着急的话,跨月计算最稳。 2. 网贷笔数多 一般来说超过5到8笔;非银行,也就是发放贷款的机构后缀里面不带银行两个字的,最好不要超过2笔,特别是小额贷款字样的,比如京东,美团,百度发放的小额贷款,这种最多允许一笔。 3.月还款金额高 严重超过月收入好多倍,一般要求是2到3倍,极个别银行5到8倍。由于网贷的还款周期短,一般会造成贷款总金额不高,但是月还款很高的情况。 4.信用卡刷爆,信用卡账户数多 信用卡使用率超过70%,经常最低还款,并且使用信用卡分期,经常使用临时额度。信用卡账户数超过8家,一般控制在6家最好。 5.逾期多 近两年单个还款账户有连续3次逾期或者累计6次(连三累六)或者逾期超过30天,甚至有的超过60天,90天。两年前的逾期影响会小一点,两年内影响比较大,但是超过90天的逾期,即使超过2年,影响也会比较大。逾期记录会保留五年,五年以后自动消失。(代偿,呆账的话需要申请征信异议消除,要不然永久存在,止付的话,注销账户就可以。)代偿怎么消除 如何申请征信异议 6.外部不良信息 诉讼,官司,酒驾,失信被执行,坐过牢,等等。 自己可以通过百行征信APP,上海市大数据中心等等免费查询系统去排查。也可以通过一些付费通道(底价是9.9元不要被忽悠了)查询自己大数据情况。 个别银行没有对接大数据系统,查不到,毕竟是少数。比如酒驾的话盛京查不到,坐过牢的,农商查不到等等。 以上情况,满足的情况越多,征信就越花。 第二步,确定自己征信花了以后,看看有没有增加征信评分的条件。 征信花了以后,征信综合评分会比较低,也就是银行常见的综合评分不足拒绝。要想在银行获得贷款,需要有一些加分项来提高征信综合评分,比如公务员、国企、事业单位、五百强、上市公司等优质单位或者说普通单位公积金交的高,个税打卡工资高,当地有资产,本科及以上学历,股票账户有余额,有公司股权等等。 满足一些加分项,就可以去申请线下人工审批的产品,人工审批一般不怎么看大数据,比如兴业消费,南银法巴,盛京银行,中信银行,温州温信贷非标,中国随心非标,农行网捷,当地农商行,中邮消费线下,中银消费线下,晋商消费线下等等,审批一笔大额期限长的贷款置换掉大部分网贷,然后养好征信,继续再做利息更低额度更高的银行置换。 假如线下人工审批也行不通,就可以考虑房产抵押或者汽车抵押贷款(有人寿保单的可以做保单质押,公积金多的可以大...

results.title: 征信花了还能去哪里贷款? - 知乎
results.summary: 征信花一样可以贷款,这里给出一点建议 1、找准自身优势 银行信用贷款,主要考察两个方面: 还款能力+还款意愿 还款能力看你的资质,还款意愿则看征信。 资质方面:主要有这几个考察点:你有多少资产、在什么单位工作、工资多少、公积金缴纳情况、学历高低,以及社会关系。 征信方面:银行会关注你的负债情况、负债率、查询次数,还有有没有逾期记录。 你得找出自己的优势所在。 比如,要是你工作单位好,就申请那些针对优质单位的贷款产品; 要是公积金缴存基数高,那就申请公积金信贷产品; 要是征信良好,就选择看重征信大数据的产品。 简单来说,就是要让银行知道你有足够的能力还钱。 2、选对贷款产品 不同银行的贷款产品,针对的人群不一样,申请条件也有差别。我们要根据自身情况,充分利用自己的优势,避开劣势。 举个例子,要是你的信用卡都刷爆了,但工作稳定,月收入 8000 元以上,一般银行要求信用卡使用率不能超过 70%,不然很可能申请贷款会被拒绝。 这种情况下,你可以试试中信银行的产品,它对信用卡使用率要求相对宽松,只要收入达标、征信查询记录不频繁就行。 这就要求我们得了解各个银行贷款产品的申请条件和风控要求。 不然,盲目申请,很可能不但贷不到款,还把自己的征信弄花了。 3、建立银行关联 这里说的关联,不是找熟人走后门,而是和银行建立业务联系。 比如,中国银行的中银 e 贷,面向的是中行的老客户,像在中行代发工资超过 6 个月的、还房贷超过 2 年的、缴存公积金 6 个月的客户。要是你有这些业务,去申请中银 e 贷,就更容易拿到额度。 和银行有业务往来,银行对你比较了解,自然更愿意给你贷款。 4、优化个人征信 在申请贷款前,先去下载一份自己的征信报告,仔细检查有没有问题。 这里有几个要注意的地方: 降低信用卡使用率: 已使用的信用卡额度,最好不要超过总额度的 70%。要是超过了,可以通过做 0 账单来解决。 清理负债: 把没用的账户注销掉,对于那些显示“余额为 0”的账户,也联系出资方把它们注销,减少负债记录。 减少贷款申请: 要是最近频繁申请贷款,建议先别着急,等 3 - 6 个月再去申请,给征信“缓一缓”。 保持信息稳定: 个人信息、居住信息、职业信息等,尽量保持一致,这能让银行觉得你比较稳定,增加贷款申请通过的概率。 控制负债率: 如果可以的话,找亲朋好友帮忙,把网贷还清,降低负债率。一般单位的人,负债最好不要超过月工资的 24 倍;优质单位的人,不要超过 36 倍。 优先线下申请: 申请贷款时,最好去线下银行网点,不要一股脑全在线上申请。线上申请如果准备不充分,很容易被拒,还白白浪费一次征信查询机会 。

results.title: 网贷多、征信花了,怎样才能申请到银行贷款? - 知乎
results.summary: 先说结论,征信花,不等于贷不了款, 但不能走常规路径,毕竟前置条件已经发生改变,你需要改策略、换方法。 下面分享几条走的通的路,都是我这几年操作上千个案例后总结出来的经验。 首先,征信花是有多花? 征信花只是个定性习惯说法,各个银行、不同产品的具体要求也不一样,很难定量。我根据实操经验可以简单划分为三个层次,大家对号入座。 1、轻度花 近半年查询12次以内,这个查询指的是你申请贷款的动作,没有逾期记录,未结清的网贷账户5个以内,这种程度还不算严重。 2、中度花 近半年查询12-30次,有逾期记录,但都结清了,信用卡使用率超70%,未结清的网贷账户5-15个,这种90%的银行信用贷款已经没戏了,资质条件非常突出的,还有机会走线下渠道,要看政策窗口、看行口关系。 3、重度花 近半年查询30次以上,信用卡刷爆,未结清的网贷账户15个以上,这种情况基本可以放弃幻想了,不优化征信是没办法做银行的信用贷款的。 3种破局的方法 1、有资产(房/车) 有资产可以做抵押贷款,不管是全款还是按揭,只有抵押物还有空间,就能做, 对网贷和征信容忍度很高。 但在实际操作中,大多数情况下只能作为一种兜底方案, 很多人并不愿意打这张牌,抵押牌打出去了,相当于人生最后的底气都堵上了。 2、优质单位 优质单位在信贷领域就是一张王牌,可以为你资质提供强而有力的背书。 银行眼中的优质单位一般指,机关单位、事业单位,国企央企等,银行青睐的香饽饽。 这是一个真实的征信花、通过人工回捞,顺利批款的案例。 在机关单位工作近10年的老领导,公积金基数1.7万,征信管理意识比较薄,用网贷用习惯了,导致征信比较花,近一个月查询16次, 自己也有尝试过申请中行随心智贷,初审就被拒了。 这个老领导资质基本面是非常扛打的,亏就亏在查询次数太多,走线上的话容易触发风控, 后来给他走了人工复议通道,补充情况说明:有消费贷需求,近期密集查询只是好奇看一下平台额度,利息太高,并没有支用。 支行行长审核后上报上级分行,顺利通过。 这里操作的关键在于,被拒后的线下渠道的人工复议,很看重行口资源、政策窗口及复议技巧,跟你自己跑到柜台填表不是一个意思,而且不是每个城市都有,需要个案个议。 3、如果是普通单位,高收入也是一张能打的牌 走的是曲线救国的路子。 普通单位+征信花,是没办法直接申请银行贷款的,那咱们可以避其锋芒,做一个对征信要求低的机构类贷款,用以过渡。 这跟普通的银行贷款有点区别, 门槛比银行低一点,比网贷高一点,相对应的,利息也比银行高一点,比网贷低一点, 属于银行和网贷之间的过渡产品,特别适合收入高,负债可控,但征信不达标的客群。 看个实操案例, 这是一个月入2w+的高收入粉丝,负债也只有20w出头,从大学开始用网贷,是一个深度网贷用户,历史贷款账户220个,当前未结清的网贷账户还有25个,但是月供高达4万,而且每个月都在各个平台之间拆借腾挪,征信上有大量密集的贷款申请记录,这在银行眼里是非常忌讳的,几乎过滤了99%的低息银行贷款,只能选择消金过渡。 最后消金批款20w,月供5k左右,还款压力前后相差8倍,这就是消金存在的价值,几乎可以说是深度网贷用户最后的接盘侠,只要你收入负债比不要太离谱就有机会。 需要注意的是,这种方案只能作为短期过渡,长期使用并不划算, 它最大的价值就是降低月供,给你争取时间去优化征信,为后期做银行贷款铺路,是一块非常好的跳板。

来源：中国青年报

# 这些年轻人用兴趣爱好解锁择业新可能
...
3月14日下午4点，32岁的许锐接女儿放学回家后，驱车赶往一个小区。他掏出手机，仔细查看订单备注：两岁，银渐层猫咪，胆小，进门先别急着找它。

这是他当天第三单上门喂宠服务。为宠物提供上门服务，他已从事6年，从一名互联网从业者，变身成为“上门铲屎官”。

许锐的经历，正是当下不少青年依托兴趣与技能开展副业、实现价值变现的缩影。这些年轻人通过副业打开人生的另一种可能，也在兴趣与爱好中不断重新定位择业与自我价值。

兴趣爱好驱动副业新起点

29岁的李娟（化名）在线上二手平台开发了自己的副业。3年前，她在社交平台发布一幅热门动漫二次创作插画，意外收获上千点赞，不少网友私信找她“接单”。

李娟从小就有绘画功底。工作之余，她常把自己创作的插画分享到社交平台。在朋友和网友鼓励下，她开始接单创作插画、壁纸与头像，慢慢把这份爱好做成一个稳定的副业。如今，李娟已在线下开设插画工作室。

在河南省洛阳市栾川县老君山脚下，24岁的冯腾龙经营一家民宿，同时接定制家具订单，而他的爱好是教客人做木工。

大学时，他迷上了做木工，喜欢制作各类小物件。如今，木工制作成为他民宿的特色“招牌”。“没想到，木工制作成为民宿的亮点，不少客人专程前来体验。”冯腾龙说，冬春景区淡季，依然有木工爱好者慕名而来，使民宿摆脱单纯“靠景吃饭”的局限，为当地旅游经济增添新活力。

闲鱼平台2025年12月发布的《数字平台中的青年新职业趋势研究（2025）》显示，过去一年共有1962万名卖家在闲鱼发布技能服务，00后占比41%，95后与90后合计约33%，本科及以上学历占比68%。超过41%的从业者副业收入占月收入30%以上，近八成有计划将副业发展为自由职业或创业项目。

一技之长踩中社会热门需求

这是他当天第三单上门喂宠服务。为宠物提供上门服务，他已从事6年，从一名互联网从业者，变身成为“上门铲屎官”。

许锐的经历，正是当下不少青年依托兴趣与技能开展副业、实现价值变现的缩影。这些年轻人通过副业打开人生的另一种可能，也在兴趣与爱好中不断重新定位择业与自我价值。

## 他試了100個副業看清真相！這5種「最賺錢」還不需要經驗
...
2026/03/19 12:20

Tom Blake嘗試過100種副業並分享經驗談。
...
〔財經頻道／綜合報導〕美媒報導，一名29歲YouTuber兼部落客分享了他從大學時期開始的副業實驗歷程，強調即便沒有經驗，也有一些副業能穩定帶來收入。自2014年開始，他嘗試超過100種副業，包括AI網站生成、加密貨幣獎勵計畫以及付費購物等，並在2018年開始經營部落格，紀錄測試結果。他如今每月透過副業賺取約2500美元（約新台幣8萬元），更分享嘗試過的100種副業當中，有5種是最賺錢的，而且不需要任何經驗。

《商業內幕》報導，Tom Blake指出，最初在2014年就讀大學時，從副業中尋求收入是為了支付學費與生活費，然而，他在Reddit上看了很多關於副業的文章，但很多都不像宣傳的那樣。2018年，這種挫敗感促使他開始寫部落格，記錄自己嘗試各種副業的經歷。此外，畢業後正職工作薪資有限，所以他依舊透過副業累積財富。

隨著時間的推移，他的部落格穩步發展。他的內容事業（Content Business）是包括YouTube頻道、部落格與電子報，最終這成為他的全職工作。透過廣告和行銷收入，最初一年收入1700美元（約新台幣5.4萬元），第三年增至2萬美元（約新台幣64萬元），累計營收超過100萬美元（約新台幣3177萬元），最終在2023年底售出。

此後，他成為數位遊牧族，靠YouTube與Substack分享副業經驗，年收達到6位數美元，每月還透過零工、賺錢網站任務、投資、諮詢與自由接案等副業，賺取約2500美元（約新台幣8萬元）。在眾多副業中，他發現5種最賺錢、最現實的副業，尤其適合初學者，且報酬相對可觀。

1.付費市場調查：透過平台如User Interviews或Respondent，參加線上焦點小組或訪談，每半小時可賺50至80美元（約新台幣1588至2541元）。

1.利基型零工App：例如Sharetown、Dolly與Lugg，處理大型退貨或搬家服務，有些地區月收入可達數千美元。

3.獎勵與探索App：下載App、玩遊戲、試用服務即可獲得報酬，雖非主要收入來源，但操作簡單且可額外賺錢。

4.AI訓練與數據標註：評估AI生成內容，部分專業項目每小時可賺25至50美元（約新台幣794至1588元），且工作量穩定。

5.網站與App測試：測試開發中網站或App，提供回饋，每次測試報酬10至100美元（約新台幣317至3170元）不等。

Tom Blake提醒，副業雖有潛力，但若宣稱「零風險高收入」，通常不可信。他建議嘗試前先查閱評論與論壇，了解真實收益與風險。他也強調，副業成功的關鍵在於持續測試與財務紀律，不僅能補貼收入，更可能為個人事業開啟全新機會。

〔財經頻道／綜合報導〕每天走路、遛狗、逛街，竟然就能賺進一筆不小的收入？英國一名精打細算的女子公開自己的「零門檻副業帳本」，，沒有專業技能、沒有創業資本，甚至在忙著搬家與度假之餘，仍在1個月內悄悄進帳超過1200英鎊（約新台幣5.2萬元）。看似零碎、毫不起眼的日常行為，被她拼湊成穩定收入。

來自英國的Natalie近日在社群平台上公開自己的副業收入來源，方法簡單到「幾乎人人都能複製」。Natalie〉在影片中表示「又一個副業滿檔的月份，我真的很開心，這個月又賺超過1000英鎊（約新台幣4.3萬元）。這個月我其實超忙，搬家、度假、工作也很滿，沒有投入太多時間在副業上，但7月我們再重新衝一波。」
...
她首先透露，透過App「Rover」賺進了363.21英鎊（約新台幣1萬5633元）。這款平台可媒合需要遛狗或寄養寵物的飼主，讓她靠照顧與遛狗就有穩定收入。此外，她也透過「WeWard」App多賺了80英鎊（約新台幣3443元），這款App只要走路就能把步數換成現金獎勵或品牌折扣。由於她本來就因遛狗而大量步行，使用這款App幾乎是「順便賺錢」。

Natalie也從事二手轉賣，將家中舊物放上eBay與Vinted販售，額外進帳38.89英鎊（約新台幣1674元）。不只如此，她還靠「CashBank」現金回饋App，在6月「被付錢逛街」，拿回317.71英鎊（約新台幣1萬3674元）。她接著補充，填寫線上問卷讓她賺進74.43英鎊（約新台幣3203元），擔任「神秘顧客」則又多拿了60.9英鎊（約新台幣2621元）。最後，加上銀行存款利息8.56英鎊（約新台幣368元），Natalie單月的額外收入總計來到1243.7英鎊（約新台幣5萬3529元）。
...

results.title: 達成財務自由的千禧世代分享4種賺錢管道 並點出最容易上手的副業類型 - Business Insider Taiwan
results.summary:
- 達成財務自由的千禧世代分享4種賺錢管道 並點出最容易上手的副業類型

財務自由作家柯迪・伯曼將副業分為四類：時間換金錢、規模化收入、共享經濟與代理商模式。他建議，對需要快速現金的初學者而言，最簡單的入門方式是直接用時間換錢。

- 柯迪・伯曼將副業分為四種類型，從快速賺取現金到可規模化的收入。
- 他表示，用時間換取金錢通常是開始快速獲利最簡單的方法。
- 如今，他專注於那些在完成前期工作後能持續產生收益的資產。

在嘗試過 超過 30 種副業（有些成功，有些失敗）後，柯迪・伯曼開發了一套他稱之為「副業框架」的系統。

這位實現財務自由的千禧世代、《30 歲退休》（Retire by 30）一書的作者告訴 Business Insider，增加額外收入的方法基本上有四種。

以下是他總結的四種副業類型，以及他認為最容易上手的類型。
...
第一種類型最直接：用時間換取金錢。這可能包括線上接案工作，例如寫作、影片或播客剪輯、架設網站或編寫電子報。也可能包括實體工作，例如園藝景觀維護、開 Uber、為 Instacart 送貨，或透過其他零工經濟平台完成任務。

伯曼表示：「你就是直接用時間來換錢。」例如：「我做這件事每小時賺 15 美元。我工作三小時，就是 45 美元。」

雖然這些副業可以快速產生現金，但代價是收入通常會隨著工作停止而結束。此外，一天只有這麼多小時。

### 第二類：可規模化的收入流

第二種類型是可規模化的收入流，也就是在初始工作完成後能持續獲利的項目。範例包括數位產品、播客、YouTube 頻道或課程。創作者可能只需花費數小時製作一次產品或內容，隨後多年便能透過銷售、贊助、聯盟行銷連結、廣告或其他變現策略持續獲利。

伯曼指出，房地產也屬於這一類，因為投資者可以購買房產並出租，然後隨著時間推移收取收入。

「第二類」副業的吸引力在於它們不完全受限於工作時數，對伯曼而言，這也是獲利最豐厚的類型。缺點是它們通常需要時間累積，才能產生可觀的收入。

他說：「你不可能今天開始經營 YouTube 頻道或開發數位產品，明天就賺到錢。但在六個月後，這些項目可能會開始帶來可觀的營收。」

### 第三類：共享經濟

第三種類型是共享經濟，涉及出租你已經擁有的資產。

這可能意味著在 Airbnb 或 Vrbo 上出租房屋或空房，透過 Turo 或 Getaround 出租汽車，或是利用平台出租儲物空間、泳池、割草設備、攝影器材、電動工具、彈跳床或充氣城堡。

伯曼說：「我看到很多人其實正守著金礦。他們可能擁有這些資產，但只是還沒將其列在平台上或進行相關設定。」

他表示，賺取額外現金並不總是意味著要從頭開始創業：「你可能只需要『啟用』一項你已經擁有的資產。」

### 第四類：代理商模式業務

他說：「這是將第一類副業轉化為某種形式的代理商。」

這種模式比親力親為更具規模化潛力，但代價是需要管理客戶與員工、定價以及品質控管。

〔財經頻道／綜合報導〕想在2026年賺更多的錢嗎？或許你已經考慮兼職，根據統計，四分之一的美國成年人都有兼職，不過還有許多人不知道從何開始兼職。

外媒《創業家》雜誌訪問8名兼職創業者，探討他們現在如何賺錢，以及如何為未來的成功做好準備。以下是8個最具創意的副業。

1. 家教

如果你是某個領域專家，而這個領域正是人們想要學習的，那麼家教輔導，無論是線上或線下，都可以成為你利用自己的知識賺取額外收入的好方法。

來自華盛頓州西雅圖的家教卡特·奧斯本 （Carter Osborne） 於2017年開始兼職做家教，以補貼研究生學費。2024年，奧斯本辭去了公關總監的工作，將他的大學論文諮詢公司Carter Osborne Tutoring轉為全職，當年收入高達22 萬美元，而他平均每週的工作時間有時只有10小時。

2. 為品牌創作內容

你是否擅長創作能夠幫助品牌病毒式傳播並吸引消費者興趣的內容？許多品牌都在投資這項服務，即用戶生成內容或用戶生成內容（UGC），而這可能成為你的下一個副業。

凱莉·羅克萊恩（Kelly Rocklein）是一位居住在俄勒岡州的企業家，她大學輟學後投身用戶生成內容領域。 2022年，羅克萊恩憑藉UGC副業實現了六位數的收入，一度在全職工作16萬美元年薪的基礎上，額外賺取了六位數的UGC收入。如今，她已轉型為創意策略顧問，專注於發展自己的公司UGC Pro。

3. 在TikTok直播轉售

如果你對收藏品或其他熱門商品充滿熱情，不妨考慮利用這種熱情開展轉售副業，例如在TikTok 或其他社交媒體平台上直播銷售商品。

馬登·福雷斯特（Madden Forrest）和他的父親史蒂文·福雷斯特最初只是出於興趣開始拆卡，購買並打開密封包裝的卡片，看看裡面有什麼。在觀看了一些TikTok部落客直播拆卡過程並向有興趣的買家出售卡片後，這對父子創業家也開始透過他們的「牛島拆卡」（Bull Island Breaks）帳號進行直播，並將業務從一天4000美元的銷售額發展到每月近5萬美元。

4. 開辦播客

這種靈活的副業不需要你走到鏡頭前與世界分享你的想法。只需找到你喜歡談論的話題，邀請一兩位嘉賓，與志同道合的廣告商合作，他們可以幫助你賺取收入，然後按下錄製鍵即可。

紐約企業家吉妮·薩拉斯瓦蒂-庫克（Ginni Saraswati-Cook）是屢獲殊榮的播客製作公司吉妮媒體的創始人兼執行長。她最初只是兼職主持自己的播客節目《吉妮秀》，後來發展成為一項全職事業。自推出以來，該公司的收入幾乎每年都翻一番，目前月收入約為5萬美元。

5. 投資網路域名

你是否擅長預測哪些網域可能賣高價？網域投資或許能成為你靈活便利的虛擬副業。

來自加州洛杉磯的丹尼斯·蒂內里諾（Dennis Tinerino）最初從事網路銷售工作，正是在那時他了解到了域名和網站建設，並由此發現了域名投資這項副業。後來，他把這項副業發展成了一項利潤豐厚的生意，每年收入高達六位數，而他每天只需投入大約一到兩個小時的工作時間。

6. 創建產品

對於有抱負的創業家來說，副業是他們在全力投入之前試水創業的絕佳方式，所以如果你有產品創意，利用空閒時間把它開發出來可能會有所回報。

# 網絡熱話｜理財達人實測100種賺錢法 推介5大「最搵錢」副業零經驗每個月多賺2萬蚊

副業/賺錢｜想透過副業增加收入，卻不知從何入手？外國一名29歲YouTuber、理財博客「This Online World」創辦人Tom Blake，自大學時期起已實測超過100種副業（Side Hustle）。他近日公開親身測試結果，盤點出5個「最賺錢且完全不需要經驗」的兼職。據悉，他現時單靠副業，每月已能穩定賺取約2,500美元（約港幣$19,550元）。
...
## 理財達人實測100種賺錢法

據外國媒體《Business Insider》報道，Tom Blake在2014年就讀大學期間，為應付學費及生活開支，開始尋找副業賺取收入。他曾在網上看到不少教人賺錢的文章，惟親身實測後發現很多都是誇大其詞，甚至暗藏陷阱。

這份屢屢「中伏」的挫敗感，促使他於2018年開設個人博客，記錄自己嘗試各種副業的經歷，當中包括AI網站生成、加密貨幣獎勵、付費購物等項目。

## 5大「最搵錢」副業

經過多年篩選與實戰，他成功將分享副業經驗的內容創作，發展為年收入達六位數美元的正職。此外，他每月仍透過各類散工及網上任務，額外賺取約$19,550港元。綜合多年實測經驗，他總結出以下5種最適合新手、無需任何經驗且回報最可觀的副業：

1.付費市場調查（Paid Market Research）

這是他認為最簡單、利潤極高的副業之一。透過報名參加「User Interviews」或「Respondent」等平台舉辦的網上焦點小組或一對一訪談，只需分享意見，每半小時就能賺取50至80美元（約港幣$391至$626）。

不過，Tom Blake亦指出，大部分申請的研究計劃均未符合相關申請條件，且每項計劃均須獨立提交申請。然而，Tom Blake分享，他平均每隔一至兩個月便能物色到一個合適的項目，工作內容相對輕鬆，壓力亦不大。

2.專門類別接案App（Niche Gig Apps）

若不怕體力勞動，這類工作實屬極具潛力之選。Tom Blake推薦多款專門處理「大型貨品退貨」及「小型搬運服務」的手機應用程式，例如外國常見的Sharetown、Dolly及Lugg等。此類勞力需求在部分地區極大，勤力的話每月收入可達數千美元，回報相當可觀。

3.獎勵與探索App（Reward & Discovery Apps）

近年獎勵類應用程式功能顯著提升，此類平台透過向使用者支付報酬的方式，鼓勵用戶下載應用程式、玩手機遊戲，以及試用各類產品與服務。

雖然不建議將其視為主要收入來源，普遍情況下每小時收益約為4至5美元（約港幣40元），但若用戶本身已有玩手遊習慣，或正考慮更換銀行戶口，此類應用仍具嘗試價值。Tom Blake指，這類平台非常適合利用乘車或觀看電視等零碎時間，輕鬆賺取額外零用錢。

4.AI訓練與數據標註（AI Training & Data Annotation）

隨著人工智能技術急速發展，市場對評估AI生成內容的需求顯著上升。不少企業會聘請人工測試員，負責審核不同模型產生的AI輸出結果並進行評分，以協助改進模型。

此類工作主要負責標註數據及訓練AI準確度，部分崗位的任務雖要求特定專業知識，但時薪可達25至50美元（約港幣$195至$391），且工作量穩定，個別職位每周更提供30至40小時的工作時間。

5.網站與App測試（Website & App Testing）

# Billionaire Hedge Fund Investor Ray Dalio Now Advises Holding a Small Amount of Bitcoin. Here's Why He's Wrong.

## Key Points

Ray Dalio recommends a small Bitcoin allocation to navigate the risk of a debt crisis.

Bitcoin tends to move in the same direction as the stock market, making it ineffective for risk reduction.

A small position could make sense for investors with a high risk tolerance.
...
Ray Dalio, founder of Bridgewater Associates, has softened his stance on Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) over the years. In 2017, he called it a bubble and said it's "not an effective storehold of wealth."

But now, in an article he published on Aug. 21, he recommended that investors hold "a bit of Bitcoin," as he believes most economies face debt and deficit problems. He considers non-government-produced money like Bitcoin to be one way to navigate this risk, and he expects it will do relatively well.
...
As far as how much "a bit" is, Dalio has previously said that allocating up to 2% of your portfolio to Bitcoin is reasonable. Even though I own Bitcoin, I disagree with Dalio's recommendation that risk mitigation is a reason to hold the cryptocurrency.

## Bitcoin doesn't reduce risk in a portfolio

Dalio recommended Bitcoin in response to a question about how investors should navigate the risk of a debt crisis and position their portfolios going forward. In fairness, he mentions gold first, with a suggested allocation of 10%-15% to reduce risk. But despite Bitcoin sometimes being called digital gold, it doesn't provide the same level of protection.

Bitcoin typically moves in the same direction as stocks. The S&P 500 and Bitcoin moved in the same direction in eight out of 10 years from 2016 through 2025, according to recent research by The Motley Fool. That includes 2022's bear market, when Bitcoin lost about three times as much as the S&P 500. If a debt crisis sends the stock market into a tailspin, Bitcoin could react similarly or even worse.

It's a different story when comparing gold versus stocks. The two tend to move in opposite directions, and in 2022, gold managed to hold its value, growing by a modest 0.3%. If you're worried about a bear market, gold is likely to help reduce losses in your portfolio more than Bitcoin would.

## Bitcoin is worth considering, but it's not a must-have

Bitcoin can be a good addition to your portfolio if you want exposure to digital assets and you have a high risk tolerance. While extremely volatile, it has had periods where it outperformed the market by a wide margin, including 2024 and 2025.

If you're interested in Bitcoin, you can invest in the cryptocurrency itself or Bitcoin ETFs, and Dalio's guideline of up to 2% Bitcoin allocation is reasonable. Experienced crypto investors may want to go a little higher and possibly branch out to other cryptocurrencies, as well, but limiting your exposure is smart with such volatile assets.

However, you can also put together a well-rounded portfolio with just stocks and bonds. And if it's risk reduction you're after, Bitcoin isn't the best choice.

# The Case for Owning Just 1 Cryptocurrency -- and Which One It Should Be
...
Most cryptocurrencies aren't worth buying.

There's one asset which has been shown to be worth owning over time.

Sometimes the simplest approach is a pretty good one.
...
Some investors who dabble in cryptocurrency end up with a portfolio like a home refrigerator that hasn't been cleaned in a long time. It'll have questionable leftovers of old tokens which were once exciting, a bunch of inert condiment-like altcoins that never did much of anything but which technically haven't expired yet, and assorted debris that looks regrettable in hindsight. There's nothing wrong with variety or diversification, but the truth is that for many investors, it's much more profitable to buy one specific coin and hold it forever.

If you're going to hold just one crypto, the case overwhelmingly favors Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) as being that one specific coin. Here's why.
...
## A small allocation can have a disproportionate effect

There are many arguments to make in favor of buying Bitcoin. The simplest argument for buying only Bitcoin is that institutional research suggests it's an easy way to improve your portfolio's performance without taking on significantly more risk.

For example, Fidelity Digital Assets published a study on March 25 examining what happens when you add Bitcoin to a standard 60/40 portfolio of stocks and bonds over a 10-year lookback period. According to that research, a traditionally diversified portfolio's return was 24% by adding an allocation of Bitcoin worth up to 10%. With an allocation of just 5%, a portfolio's annualized returns were 17.5%. A portfolio without any of the coin had annualized returns of around 9.4%, though it was also slightly less volatile and also had a slightly more favorable maximum drawdown level.

Research by BlackRock from late 2024 also supports the idea that a 1% to 2% allocation to Bitcoin can give portfolios significant exposure to upside, and at a manageable level of downside risk. A slightly earlier investigation by Grayscale suggests that the sweet spot for Bitcoin allocation is roughly 5% of a portfolio's value for maximizing its risk-adjusted returns.

## Other cryptocurrencies don't have the same value proposition

You don't need much Bitcoin to shift a portfolio's return profile meaningfully. That means that if it's the only crypto you buy, you'll be exposed to the upside you're likely looking for, and you won't need to worry about researching or holding other cryptocurrencies.

Even if you did think about buying other cryptoassets, it's important to notice that they don't offer the same features to a portfolio as Bitcoin does. Cryptos like Ethereum and XRP both have strong investment theses, but neither one has the elegant simplicity of Bitcoin's tightly constrained supply policy, nor do they have the luxury of being scarce stores of value. While they might grow faster, they need to constantly change and compete with alternative investments in the crypto sector in a way that Bitcoin simply doesn't.

So if you're going to be a one-crypto investor, make sure it's Bitcoin.

# Bitcoin May Now Be More Attractive Than Gold Long-Term, Says JPMorgan Strategist
...
Bitcoin has gotten hammered this year, while gold has performed well.

Investors are clearly questioning Bitcoin's digital gold narrative.

However, strategists at JPMorgan see long-term upside for Bitcoin.
...
It's been a rough go for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), the world's largest cryptocurrency by market cap, which is now down nearly 22% on the year, despite a strong rally on Feb. 6.

Investors seem to be questioning whether Bitcoin is truly a form of digital Gold, with its finite supply of 21 million tokens, and whether it can therefore serve as a hedge against currency debasement and inflation.
...
However, for those who follow Bitcoin and crypto, big sell-offs and steep bear markets should be nothing new, as they tend to occur every few years. Despite the big sell-off and investors asking serious questions, strategists at JPMorgan Chase see a compelling long-term opportunity that could make Bitcoin even more attractive than gold.

## Bitcoin has relatively low volatility compared to gold

Gold has surged as investors have worried about a lower dollar from years of intense money printing and a mounting pile of U.S. government debt. Furthermore, there have been many geopolitical concerns and concerns about the Federal Reserve's independence. Bitcoin seemed to follow gold higher last year, but this year has decoupled from the precious metal thus far, although Gold (NYSEMKT: GLD) has also struggled as of late.

"[Cryptocurrencies] came under further pressure over the past week as risk assets and in particular tech came under pressure and as gold and silver, the other perceived hedges to a catastrophic scenario, saw a sharp correction," a team of JPMorgan analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou wrote in a research note published yesterday.

Interestingly, Panigirtzoglou also noted that while gold has risen much more than Bitcoin since October, it has done so with much higher volatility, making Bitcoin "even more attractive compared to gold."

Panigirtzoglou theorizes that if Bitcoin's volatility were to equal gold's, its price would soar to $266,000 per token, implying significant upside from Bitcoin's current price of below $69,000 per token, as of this writing. Panigirtzoglou does not see this materializing in the near term, but it shows how Bitcoin could still be a potential long-term safe haven.

The crux of the digital gold debate is that Bitcoin often trades like a high-beta tech stock. Software stocks have gotten crushed, and that has spilled into Bitcoin and crypto.

While things seem difficult, I do think investors should remember that Bitcoin has survived multiple drawdowns of over 90% only to make new highs each time, so I think the token can bounce back over the long term. The verdict on digital gold remains to be seen, but Bitcoin has strong potential to serve as a unique diversifier in a multi-asset portfolio, so it's worth allocating at least a little capital to it.

## Does bitcoin provide portfolio diversification?

Diversification is a core investment principle that involves allocating invested capital across various asset classes, sectors or geographic regions to reduce the overall risk of the portfolio. It is a risk-management strategy that is intended to limit exposure to the performance of any single investment by investing in a broad range of asset classes that have a low or negative correlation. For example, instead of purchasing a single stock or index exchange-traded fund (ETF), an investor might diversify the portfolio by purchasing a mixture of large- and small-cap stocks, international stocks, bonds, commodities, and a certain percentage of cash. Investing offers both the potential for returns as well as risk, and diversification is meant to hedge the potential risk from investing in a single asset. However, it should also be understood that diversification does not guarantee a profit or protect against loss of principal during periods of broad market selloffs.

Is Bitcoin an effective portfolio diversifier? If so, this would suggest that it historically has a low or negative correlation with traditional assets such as stocks or bonds. The answer may depend upon the timeframe and stock/bond composition, but based on our research, from January 2015 through October 2025 there appears to be only a moderate correlation between bitcoin and equities and a relatively low correlation with core bonds. While not a negative or low-correlation asset, Bitcoin can still provide some diversification benefit.

## Is bitcoin a good trading vehicle?

A speculative asset is sometimes identified as a nonproductive asset, exhibiting high price volatility and offering the potential for both substantial gains and losses (high risk/reward) in a relatively short period of time. Generally, speculators are active market participants who seek to earn a profit from anticipated near-term price volatility of an asset, be it higher or lower. Conversely, fundamental investors are generally patient, perform due diligence on investment opportunities, and hope to grow their wealth over time through both price appreciation and income. So where does bitcoin fall on the spectrum of investing?

On the one hand, bitcoin's historical price volatility suggests that it belongs in the category of speculation. Bitcoin's beta, which is a measure of volatility relative to a benchmark such as the S&P 500 index, has been relatively high, suggesting large relative movements both higher and lower. Bitcoin's roller-coaster ride over the past decade has provided ample opportunities to play both sides of abrupt price swings, which suggests that it can be a good trading vehicle for speculators. However, its historical price appreciation and potential to find more utility within the economy in the future increasingly have attracted the interest of institutional and longer-term focused investors. Cryptocurrency enthusiasts believe that bitcoin provides more than just price volatility, such as potentially acting as a hedge against currency debasement or as a widely adopted decentralized medium of exchange.

# Should You Own Bitcoin in 2026? A Wealth Advisor’s View

## What Is Happening With Bitcoin?

Bitcoin has been a frequent topic of client conversations recently. That makes sense. The price action has been confusing, the headlines are loud, and the opinions range from “digital gold for the next century” to “it is going to zero”.

Cutting through the noise requires a clear framework.

Start with the basics. Cryptocurrency in general and Bitcoin in particular are an emerging high-risk, high-potential-return asset class. Bitcoin is three to five times as volatile as the S&P 500 stock index. That is the reality, and it should shape every decision made around how much of it belongs in a portfolio and why.

Now, what has happened? Bitcoin staged a very powerful rally into the fall of 2025. What followed was unusual: there was almost no follow-through. Returns since that rally have been disappointing.

Several forces are likely at work. The “halving cycle” narrative—the idea that Bitcoin follows a predictable four-year pattern tied to its supply schedule—gets cited frequently as an explanation. It is probably not the real mechanism. Bitcoin supply changes are modest and well-telegraphed; markets price known information in advance. The more likely drivers are a contraction/stagnation in global liquidity and a pullback in risk appetite. Add macro headwinds and regulatory uncertainty caused by delays in passing the Clarity Act, and the disappointing returns make sense.

The Clarity Act is the key piece of legislation that would establish a formal regulatory framework for digital assets. It has not passed through both houses of Congress. That matters because institutional capital moves slowly and carefully, and without regulatory clarity, many large allocators are reluctant to increase their exposure. Until that legislation passes, a meaningful source of potential buying pressure remains on the sidelines.

The macro backdrop has also not helped. Tariff-driven trade uncertainty, geopolitical risk, and an unpredictable interest rate environment have all worked to push investors toward caution. When risk appetite contracts across the board, high-volatility assets like Bitcoin tend to feel it first and feel it hardest. The result has been a measurable shift in investor sentiment away from speculative positioning.

## Why the Outlook Is More Encouraging Than the Price Suggests?

Underneath the surface the picture is more encouraging than the price suggests.

The signs of institutional adoption are real and growing. JP Morgan, BlackRock, Fidelity, and Goldman Sachs (amongst others) have all adopted blockchain technology and are building products centred on Bitcoin. Morgan Stanley is now publicly advising its wealth management clients to allocate up to 4% in Bitcoin. The United States is actively discussing the establishment of a strategic Bitcoin reserve. Finally, Bitcoin is beginning to find use cases inside the artificial intelligence economy.

Deeply cautious sentiment has historically been a reliable forward-looking positive for risk assets. It signals that the aggressive selling has already happened and that weak hands have largely been shaken out. Bitcoin at a 50% discount from its 2025 peak, in an environment where almost nobody is enthusiastic, looks different than Bitcoin at all-time highs with excited investors.

## How Much Bitcoin Belongs in a Portfolio?

None of this guarantees results. Taken together, these signs argue that Bitcoin is not being abandoned. The foundation is being built, even if the price has not reflected it yet.

So where does that leave us from a portfolio perspective?

The approach here is to treat Bitcoin as an emerging asset class—one with a small place in a well-constructed portfolio. An allocation in the range of 1% to 2% is the right size for most clients. Big enough that if Bitcoin produces anything close to its historical returns, it generates a meaningful tailwind. Small enough that if it went to zero tomorrow, it would not derail an otherwise strong year.

The other thing worth remembering when considering high-risk, high-potential return investments is this: the goal is not to find the perfect entry point. The goal is to decide whether there is an opportunity worth participating in and size it appropriately. Process beats prediction in Bitcoin just like everywhere else.

If you have questions about how Bitcoin fits your specific situation, reach out.

## Bitcoin adds outsize risk to a portfolio

Bitcoin’s unique characteristics make it difficult to classify using traditional asset allocation frameworks. It offers the potential for capital appreciation and some degree of currency diversification, but it also introduces significant risk.

Here’s how a bitcoin allocation compares to other diversifiers and may affect your portfolio’s risk:

- Bitcoin versus gold. While their correlations to traditional multi-asset portfolios have been similarly low, their contributions to overall portfolio risk have been vastly different. Our analysis has shown that since the launch of bitcoin ETFs in January 2024, a 5% allocation to gold alongside a traditional 60/40 portfolio would have contributed 2% to overall portfolio risk. The same allocation to bitcoin would have contributed 13% of portfolio risk.
- Bitcoin versus fixed income. A similar exercise shows that historically, the 40% bond allocation in a classic 60/40 accounted for only about 9% of the portfolio’s total risk. Allocating 3.5% to bitcoin introduced the same level of risk as the entire 40% fixed income allocation.

## A moderate allocation to bitcoin contributes about 2x–3x its weight in risk

### Contribution to risk, %

For ultra-conservative portfolios or near-term funds, even a small bitcoin allocation may introduce unacceptable volatility and drawdown risk. Aggressive or opportunistic investors may consider sizing bitcoin within their risk budgets, but careful sizing and risk management are essential.

## Bitcoin doesn’t exist in a vacuum

The digital asset landscape is rapidly evolving, and bitcoin is only one part of it. Tokenization—the representation of real-world assets as digital tokens on a blockchain7—is broadening access to alternative investments and streamlining asset management. Blockchains now function as settlement rails for transferring and recording asset ownership, enabling instant, transparent and cost-effective value transfers across global markets.

Since January 2025, financial institutions’ adoption of blockchain-based products and strategies has accelerated.8 As investors become more familiar and comfortable with the technological ecosystem bitcoin inhabits, adoption of the coin may accelerate.

And as the digital asset ecosystem beyond bitcoin expands, new opportunities and risks to bitcoin’s progress may also rise. The increasing adoption of USD-pegged stablecoins, to take one commonly cited example, could reinforce the dollar’s dominance. The USD peg could help provide more efficient and secure cross-border transactions and settlement. Yet it could also slow the broader de-dollarization trend of the past year and work against wider crypto adoption.9

## Why we don’t favor a core allocation

Bitcoin is still on its journey from digital curiosity to widely used asset. While we currently do not recommend bitcoin as part of a core portfolio, it may suit aggressive and/or speculative investors as a satellite allocation, if they’re willing to accept its risks and volatility. Bitcoin has shown its potential for significant returns in the past, but future outcomes remain uncertain, so careful sizing and risk awareness are essential.

Beyond bitcoin, the digital asset ecosystem is evolving rapidly. As new technologies and platforms develop, they may help build the infrastructure cryptocurrencies need—for broader market acceptance, and to win our confidence, as well.

# New report: Bitcoin’s role within an institutional portfolio

April 8, 2026
...
This article is an introduction to the latest 21shares macro report.
...
Since 2008, the global monetary landscape has undergone a structural shift. What began as an "extraordinary" $600 billion quantitative easing program is now a permanent fixture of central banking, with the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet standing at approximately $6.6 trillion in early 2026.

In our latest report, 21shares Head of Macro Stephen Coltman examines how, amid this era of persistent debt expansion, Bitcoin has transitioned from a fringe experiment into an institutional asset class – offering a potential tool for both return enhancement and portfolio diversification.

## Three institutional pillars

Bitcoin’s role within an institutional portfolio explains three structural drivers shaping bitcoin’s value proposition:

- Dual exposure: Bitcoin captures both technological adoption and inflation trends. It maintains a positive beta to the tech sector while its fixed supply provides a hedge against fiat debasement.
- Systemic tail hedge: As an asset without counterparty risk, bitcoin is nobody’s liability. During the 2023 banking crisis, bitcoin’s correlation to banking stocks flipped negative, rallying 30% as traditional systems faced liquidity strains.
- Rebalancing alpha: Bitcoin’s volatility is an opportunity. Systematic rebalancing allows investors to harvest "volatility alpha," converting price swings into a smoother path of excess returns.

## Diversification and strategy

The report also outlines the high concentration risk a typical 60/40 portfolio currently faces, with roughly 25% of the equity exposure tied to just eight US tech giants. Integrating a modest 3% bitcoin allocation provides valuable diversification.

Our data through February 2026 suggest that a rebalanced 3% allocation can increase annual returns by 0.5% to 0.7% with only a marginal increase in volatility, yielding a Sharpe ratio near 1 for the incremental performance.

## The long-term outlook

Where to from here? With daily trading volumes exceeding $50 billion, bitcoin now rivals the liquidity of mega-cap equities like Nvidia. As developed economies face mounting fiscal pressures, we believe that bitcoin serves as a critical insurance policy against the "gradually and then suddenly" fracturing of the traditional monetary order.

# The Gen Z Playbook for Making Money Fast in 2026

Everyone is trying to make more money right now just to keep up with the breakneck rate at which costs seem to be going up. However, making money fast is a top priority for Gen Z as they are just starting out and have no financial foundation to battle rising rent, student loans and grocery bills.

This is why more young adults are looking for ways to make quick cash without committing to a second full‑time job. Fortunately, in 2026, there are more opportunities than ever to put some bigger chunks of change in your pocket, thanks to assists from AI tools and flexible online work.

The key isn’t just working harder, it’s also about working smarter with strategies that actually pay off fast. Here are a few sneaky (but effective) ways Gen Z can make quick cash, whether you need money this week or want to build a steady side income.

## 1. Refer Family and Friends and Get Funds

Many companies, from banks to clothing stores, pay their customers to help them drum up new business, and you can cash in on the opportunity. You can even use AI to help maximize this process, as those tools have completely changed the side hustle game.

# 5 Fastest Ways To Make Extra Money from What You Already Know How to Do

Making extra money isn't difficult. It's a lot easier than you might think. You can earn more money by leveraging what you already know and turning it into a business venture. You'd be surprised by the amount of people willing to pay for your expertise or skills.

Not convinced or unsure how to go about doing this? Let's look at some of the fastest ways you can earn extra money from what you already know how to do.

## Tutoring

If you're an expert in your field or know how to do something well, you can quickly earn extra money by tutoring. Popular tutoring subjects include STEM subjects, college prep courses and computer science. You can use third-party websites to list your tutoring availability and start lining up clients with barely any start-up costs besides a laptop. Over time, you can raise your rates and build up your client list to really pull in extra money.

## Online Classes

Like tutoring, teaching an online class is a fast way to earn extra money by sharing what you know with others. You can do this through an online school provider or by creating your online course and selling it to others. Setting up an online course will take more time and effort than tutoring since you'll need to create lesson plans and record yourself teaching. Once it's all setup, though, it can be a great source of passive income.

## Selling Products

Are you artistically inclined and make art for fun? People may be willing to buy the things you create as a hobby. You can list your products for sale through an online marketplace like Etsy. The marketplace makes it easy by facilitating transactions and assisting in advertising. Once your shop is up and running, you only need to worry about creating and shipping the products to paying customers.

## Sell Your Skills

Selling physical products isn't the only fast way to make money from a hobby. You can also profit by selling the skills you have. Maybe you're good at photography or are a talented singer. You can easily make money by taking others' pictures or earn tips from booking singing gigs at your local bar or restaurant.

## Monetize Your Blog or Social Media

Writing a blog about what you know or talking about it on social media platforms can help you earn money with minimal effort. Some blog websites like Substack allow subscribers to pay for the content you publish, so if you can write compelling posts about things you are confident about, people may be willing to pay to read about it. Likewise, if you can confidently talk about what you are passionate about and build a loyal subscribership, platforms like YouTube will share the advertising revenue they make from your videos, or you can charge for channel memberships.

With one solid idea, heaps of enthusiasm, and a commitment to keep going when it’s tough, you can start a side project that soon becomes your full time gig. It’s go time.

Each of these ideas can be set up with zero capital, just a laptop and internet connection. You can sign up potential clients by telling your existing network what you’re doing and asking them to tell their friends, or you can start messaging people on LinkedIn. It doesn’t matter how you do it. What matters is that you start.

Replace your salary with freelance work: business ideas to start today

LinkedIn ghostwriter

Everyone wants to be famous for their work. LinkedIn now has over a billion users, but most people don’t even post. Be the person who helps others show up. Learn how to grow a personal brand and business on LinkedIn. Understand content psychology, the structure of a winning post, and how to drive engagement and generate leads.

It’s not that hard. And people want the service. Once you understand how it works, create a monthly package to represent someone on LinkedIn. Charge $1500 a month, get 3 clients, and you’ve replaced your salary. For each person you could do a daily post, daily engagement, and report on their growth each month. Throw in inbox management and speak to their prospects in their voice for extra value. Each client might take you 60-90 minutes every day and the rest of your time is yours to use as you please.

Automation creator

Too much to do and not enough time? You’re not alone. Most people have this problem. Automation could solve all their problems but they don’t know how to set it up. That’s where you come in. Learn how to use automation tools like Zapier, Make, Relevance and Airtable. Meet potential clients, understand their business, then turn their manual processes into ones that run without them being there.

Automation is serious business, and the value is clear. You could create a $2500 setup offer and secure two a month to replace your salary. You could run classes and workshops to teach others how to use the skills you just learned. You don’t need to be a longtime expert, you just need to be a few steps ahead. Learn, teach, repeat. Test your skills with your own work then show others the way.

Professional fixer

My VA is more than a VA. She’s a fixer. That means she fixes me up with everything I need at any given time. She books appointments, she researches places I go before I get there. She organises trips and schedules my content. Everyone needs a person like this.
...
Could you be someone’s fixer? Six clients, each paying you $750 a month, where you’re on hand to organise whatever they need. Gym memberships, gifts for their friends, guest lists, online shopping and spreadsheets. Skills required: being responsive, being fast, being resourceful enough to get things done and audacious enough to ask questions and take action. You might just love taking care of someone’s world.

Video editor

Everyone is building their personal brand so they are creating more content than ever. Videos are no longer big budget, high production feats that take ages to produce. Content is more disposable. If you can learn video editing software, you can be someone’s on demand editor, creating them regular assets to grow their profile online.

Nine clients at $500 a month each will replace your salary. Do a good job, and they’ll tell their friends. Learn how to use Descript and Final Cut Pro and increase your hard drive capacity. Add “video editor” to your LinkedIn headline and start messaging entrepreneurs. Get one client then ask for a testimonial and share examples of your work with everyone else you meet. This is totally possible to do full time and it’s possible for you within a year.

Accountability partner

Where would you be if you did everything you ever said you were going to do? You’d be flying high, earning millions, and reading this article from your private yacht. But people don’t do everything they say they will do. They go off track, get distracted, and convince themselves they aren’t capable of greatness. Become an accountability partner to people who want to stop being held back. People who want to break their limits, hit new milestones, and go beyond their excuses to see what is possible.

Charge $250 a month for weekly check-ins and regular cheerleading....

# A financially independent millennial breaks down 4 ways to bring in cash, and shares the easiest type of hustle to start with

Cody Berman categorizes side hustles into four types, from quick cash to scalable income.

He says trading time for money is often the easiest way to start earning fast.

Today, he focuses on assets that can keep earning after the upfront work is done.

After trying more than 30 side hustles — some hits, some flops — Cody Berman has developed what he calls a "side hustle framework."

There are essentially four ways to bring in extra income, the financially independent millennial and author of "Retire by 30" told Business Insider.

Here are his four types of side hustles, plus the one he says is the easiest to start.

### Type 1:
...
The first type is the most straightforward:
...
That could mean online freelance work, such as writing, video or podcast editing, website building, or compiling email newsletters. It could also mean in-person work, such as landscaping, driving for Uber, delivering for Instacart, or completing tasks through other gig-economy platforms.

"You're just straight up trading your time for money," Berman said. For example: "I make $15 an hour doing this. I work three hours, that's $45."

While these side hustles can start producing cash quickly, the trade-off is that income generally ends when the work ends. Plus, there are only so many hours in a day.

### Type 2: Scalable income streams

The second type is a scalable income stream — something that can continue earning after the initial work is done. Examples include a digital product, podcast, YouTube channel, or course. A creator might spend hours making a product or piece of content once, then continue earning through sales, sponsorships, affiliate links, ads, or other monetization strategies for years.

Real estate also fits into this bucket, Berman said, because an investor can buy a property, get it rented, and then collect income over time.

The appeal of "type two" side hustles is that they're not strictly tied to hours worked — and, for Berman, they've been the most lucrative. The trade-off is that they typically take time to build before they produce meaningful income.

"You're not going to start a YouTube channel or create a digital product today and make money with either of those things tomorrow," he said. "But in six months' time, those things might start making serious income."

### Type 3: Sharing economy

The third type, the sharing economy, involves renting out assets you already own.

That could mean listing a house or spare room on Airbnb or Vrbo, renting out a car through Turo or Getaround, or using platforms that let people rent out storage space, pools, lawn equipment, photography equipment, power tools, trampolines, or bounce houses.

"I see so many people who are just sitting on gold mines," Berman said. "They might have this asset, but they just haven't listed it or set it up for one of those platforms."

Bringing in extra cash doesn't always mean building a business from scratch, he said: "You just might need to 'turn on' one of the assets that you already own."

### Type 4: Agency-style businesses

The final type is what Berman calls a hybrid model: turning a time-for-money side hustle into an agency-style business. For example, someone might start as a freelance writer, charge clients by the project, and hire other writers to help complete the work. Or someone might start as a dog walker, then grow it into a dog-walking company by hiring other walkers.

"This is taking a type-one side hustle and basically turning it into an agency of some sort," he said.

The model can be more scalable than doing all the work yourself, but the trade-off is that it requires managing clients and employees, pricing, and quality control.

### The easiest way to get started

When Berman was trying to leave his corporate job in 2018, he started with type-one side hustles.

He took on freelance projects, including writing newsletters, editing videos and podcasts, and managing affiliate programs.

"It was literally anything that I could do to make money trading my time," he said.

At the same time, he was building type-two income streams, including a blog, podcast, and digital products business. Those took longer to start profiting, but today they are among his largest sources of income.

"Today, I exclusively focus on these type-two-style hustles, where I am creating something, building something, buying something that is going to pay me in perpetuity," he said.

results.summary:
Trial: When user signs up for a free trial of a product or service.

“Pixel Fires”: This is what happens when someone clicks on your link (they become a lead).

US/FR/CA: Offer only valid in that specific country.

AM: Stands for “Affiliate Manager”. Your AM is your go-to person in the network

Sale or Rev Share: You get a cut of every sale (one-time or recurring).

When you see an offer that looks good, click on the listing:

Then, check out the details. The listing will usually give you key information on the offer, like what the user needs to do and what type of traffic is allowed:

If the offer looks good, hit the “Full Landing Page Preview” button. This will show you the page that users will see when they click on your link:

So:

What should you look for in a landing page?

First, you want a landing page that looks clean and professional.

If it looks shady to you, it’ll look shady to your traffic too… and it won’t convert.

Also, the more fields a page has, the lower your conversion rate is going to be.

That said:

More fields also mean higher commissions.

So don’t be automatically turned off by a page like this that requires 6 steps:

If the traffic is motivated enough (for example, they your traffic comes from people searching in Google for “best online degrees”), I’ve found that they’ll fill out just about anything.

“What if I can’t find an offer?”

Depending on your niche, you may not be able to find an offer that fits your site’s topic.

If that’s the case, you want to look for CPA offers that appeal to your traffic’s demographic.

Let me illustrate what I mean with a real life example…

I used to run a site in the “dating” niche that was getting 2,000 visitors per day.

I put “dating” in quotes because it was comprised mostly of 9th graders wondering how to talk to Sally that sits in the back.

(Not the type of stuff that’s easy to monetize)

Despite the fact that I tested about 20 different themes and ad placements, I wasn’t making ANY money with Adsense.

And when I looked at the ads Adsense was putting on my site, I realized that they weren’t dating related at all.

Instead, they were targeted based on demographics.

That’s when I decided to switch out Adsense for an email/zip submit offer for a free Xbox 360.

And just like, that I started to make significantly more money than I was making from Adsense.

## Step #2: Join a network

If the offer looks good, it’s time to join the network that runs the offer. You can apply by clicking on the “Join Network” link on the offer page:

When you do, you’ll see an application like this:

I should point something out:

You’ll be asked to provide a phone number… which they will call.

This is a stumbling block for a lot of people. As affiliate marketers we’re accustomed to making money online without having to talk to anyone.

But the reality of CPA is this:

If you want to join a CPA network, you’ll need to talk to someone on the phone. You may have to even fill out some actual paperwork. It’s no big deal.

How to get accepted by any network

Remember that CPA networks aren’t trying to make things difficult. They just want to make sure that you’re a legit business that will send them real leads (which you are).

So it’s just a matter of being transparent.

Here are some tips that will help you get accepted:

- Call them before they call you: Shady affiliates try to fly under the radar screen. So give the network a call right after you apply. This shows you’re the real deal. I was accepted into one network literally 10 minutes after applying. How? I picked up the phone and called.
- Check uour Whois: Some networks check to see if your site’s whois address matches your mailing address.
- Be honest: Most applications have a section to learn more about your online marketing experience

Remember: you don’t need to be an internet marketing rockstar to get accepted.

In fact, I joined my first affiliate network when I was making about $20/day from Adsense. They just want you to put honest answers into these fields.

So if you’re new to affiliate marketing, it’s OK to tell them that.

### 6. UGC creator quick gigs

UGC (user-generated content) is when you create short, “native-looking” videos and photos that brands use in ads or on social media. In 2026, many companies prefer UGC over polished studio ads because it feels more authentic and converts better, so demand stays high. Rate benchmarks vary, but many creators price UGC per video, often with add-ons for usage rights or extra hooks.

How to get started fast

- Pick 1–2 categories you can shoot at home (skincare, fitness, apps, food, gadgets).
- Build a mini portfolio: 3 sample videos (15–30 seconds) filmed on your phone.
- Offer “1 script + 1 video + 2 variations” as a simple starter package.

If you charge $200 per video and deliver 3 videos in a week, that’s $600 (plus potential add-ons like extra revisions or extended usage). 2026 pricing guides commonly show per-video ranges that move up with experience and licensing.

Many UGC deals pay after delivery/approval, with timing depending on the contract. To avoid delays, use clear milestones (deposit → first cut → final files) and invoice right away.

Tips to land gigs faster

- Lead with results-focused hooks (“3 angles for your next ad”).
- Offer a 48-hour turnaround option with a rush fee.
- Keep your deliverables simple: raw + edited + captions.

## Selling digital products

Print-on-demand (POD) merchandise and stock photos are quick-to-launch digital products that can be listed for sale almost instantly. Selling digital products like these often involves minimal upfront costs, offering a relatively low financial commitment compared to traditional inventory-based businesses.

### 7. Print-on-demand merchandise

POD is a business model where your designs are printed on products like t-shirts, hoodies, or phone cases only after someone places an order. It’s a low-risk way to sell custom items without holding inventory.

No design experience? No problem. You can start a POD business by buying ready-made designs on sites like Etsy. For example, there’s a bundle with 25,000 anime graphics for just $3.

Once you have your designs, the next step is to place them on products using a print-on-demand platform like Printful, Spring, or Society6.

These platforms let you choose an item – like a t-shirt or mug – and upload your design to see how it will look.

You can adjust the size and placement, then save it as a finished product listing. The whole process usually takes just a few minutes per item, so you can have your first product ready to sell in under an hour.

With a low initial investment, you can profit by pricing your products with a markup of 30% to 50% above cost.

For example, if it costs $15 to produce a hoodie, you could price it between $22.50 to $30 and keep the difference as profit.

POD platforms typically pay out earnings anywhere from 10 days to once a month.

### 8. Stock photo/video sales

Selling stock photos and videos can be a quick and lucrative side hustle if you already have a sizable collection of high-quality content.

How much you can earn depends on factors like the quality of your images, how well you use keywords, and how many stock photo websites you upload to.

For example, photographer Peter Orsel earned about $1,900 in his first year of stock photography, uploading around 4,500 photos across various platforms.

To maximize your earnings from stock photos and videos, focus on taking practical images that businesses actually need, such as “a person typing at a desk” or “a team in a meeting.” These types of images tend to sell more frequently than artsy or abstract shots.

Peter also recommends uploading consistently even if you’re not completely satisfied with a shot, as you never know what buyers are looking for.

Once you have your images ready, upload them to popular stock platforms like Shutterstock, iStockPhoto, Dreamstime, 123RF, and Adobe Stock.

Dreamstime is notable for offering faster payouts once you reach a $100 earnings balance, while the other platforms typically pay on a monthly basis.

- 達成財務自由的千禧世代分享4種賺錢管道 並點出最容易上手的副業類型

財務自由作家柯迪・伯曼將副業分為四類：時間換金錢、規模化收入、共享經濟與代理商模式。他建議，對需要快速現金的初學者而言，最簡單的入門方式是直接用時間換錢。

- 柯迪・伯曼將副業分為四種類型，從快速賺取現金到可規模化的收入。
- 他表示，用時間換取金錢通常是開始快速獲利最簡單的方法。
- 如今，他專注於那些在完成前期工作後能持續產生收益的資產。

在嘗試過 超過 30 種副業（有些成功，有些失敗）後，柯迪・伯曼開發了一套他稱之為「副業框架」的系統。

這位實現財務自由的千禧世代、《30 歲退休》（Retire by 30）一書的作者告訴 Business Insider，增加額外收入的方法基本上有四種。

以下是他總結的四種副業類型，以及他認為最容易上手的類型。
...
第一種類型最直接：用時間換取金錢。這可能包括線上接案工作，例如寫作、影片或播客剪輯、架設網站或編寫電子報。也可能包括實體工作，例如園藝景觀維護、開 Uber、為 Instacart 送貨，或透過其他零工經濟平台完成任務。

伯曼表示：「你就是直接用時間來換錢。」例如：「我做這件事每小時賺 15 美元。我工作三小時，就是 45 美元。」

雖然這些副業可以快速產生現金，但代價是收入通常會隨著工作停止而結束。此外，一天只有這麼多小時。

### 第二類：可規模化的收入流

第二種類型是可規模化的收入流，也就是在初始工作完成後能持續獲利的項目。範例包括數位產品、播客、YouTube 頻道或課程。創作者可能只需花費數小時製作一次產品或內容，隨後多年便能透過銷售、贊助、聯盟行銷連結、廣告或其他變現策略持續獲利。

伯曼指出，房地產也屬於這一類，因為投資者可以購買房產並出租，然後隨著時間推移收取收入。

「第二類」副業的吸引力在於它們不完全受限於工作時數，對伯曼而言，這也是獲利最豐厚的類型。缺點是它們通常需要時間累積，才能產生可觀的收入。

他說：「你不可能今天開始經營 YouTube 頻道或開發數位產品，明天就賺到錢。但在六個月後，這些項目可能會開始帶來可觀的營收。」

### 第三類：共享經濟

第三種類型是共享經濟，涉及出租你已經擁有的資產。

這可能意味著在 Airbnb 或 Vrbo 上出租房屋或空房，透過 Turo 或 Getaround 出租汽車，或是利用平台出租儲物空間、泳池、割草設備、攝影器材、電動工具、彈跳床或充氣城堡。

伯曼說：「我看到很多人其實正守著金礦。他們可能擁有這些資產，但只是還沒將其列在平台上或進行相關設定。」

他表示，賺取額外現金並不總是意味著要從頭開始創業：「你可能只需要『啟用』一項你已經擁有的資產。」

### 第四類：代理商模式業務

最後一種類型是伯曼所稱的混合模式：將「時間換金錢」的副業轉變為代理商模式的業務。例如，某人可能從自由撰稿人開始，按計畫向客戶收費，並聘請其他作家協助完成工作。或者某人可能從遛狗員開始，然後透過聘請其他遛狗員將其發展成一家遛狗公司。

他說：「這是將第一類副業轉化為某種形式的代理商。」

這種模式比親力親為更具規模化潛力，但代價是需要管理客戶與員工、定價以及品質控管。

### 最容易上手的入門方式

當伯曼在 2018 年試圖離開企業職位時，他是從第一類副業開始的。

他承接了各種自由接案計畫，包括編寫電子報、剪輯影片和播客，以及管理聯盟行銷計畫。

他說：「當時只要是能用時間換錢的事，我幾乎什麼都做。」

## 

### How do lenders decide whether to offer someone a credit card?

Lenders will look at several factors when deciding whether to offer you a card. These include:

Your income – you’ll need to give details of your annual salary and any other earnings.

Your credit score – a hard credit check is carried out to find out how well (or otherwise) you look after debt today, and how successful (or otherwise) you’ve been at doing it in the past.

The amount of debt you have – it can be a red flag if you’re already juggling a lot of debt. Lenders want to be sure you can manage a new card without overstretching your finances.

You may be rejected for a credit card if you have a poor credit history. Lenders will look at this as part of their assessment of the likelihood you’ll repay what you owe.

## Credit card FAQs

### Am I eligible for a credit card?

Usually, applying to a lender is the only way to work out whether you'll be accepted for a card. Yet that marks your credit file, and could affect your ability to get credit in future. Our eligibility calculator uses a 'soft search' to calculate and show your chances of acceptance before you apply, meaning you can protect your credit score from too many needless applications.

### How do I apply for a credit card?

Once you decide which credit card is best for you, you’ll need to provide some basic details such as your name, address, income, and outgoings. Some cards might also ask about existing debts. The application itself only takes a few minutes, and you'll usually know if you’ve been approved within a day or two.

If you're accepted, your physical card will typically arrive within five to 10 working days. But don't worry if you need access sooner – many providers offer digital cards, so you can start using your credit straight away through your phone's wallet app, even before your card lands in the post.

Get more details on how to apply for a credit card.

### How do lenders decide whether to give you a credit card?

You'll need to pass a credit check to get a credit card. This lets the lender work out how 'risky' you are to lend to, and takes into account your income and other financial commitments. It can then either accept or decline you.

The criteria differs between lenders – you could be accepted by one but declined by another. So it’s better to use an eligibility checker to see your chances of acceptance before applying.

If you go on to apply, any application will leave a mark on your credit report, even if you're declined, which could affect your ability to get credit in future (this is especially true if you make multiple applications in a short time period). Read our guide to how credit scoring works for full info.

### What are the pros and cons of owning a credit card?

Credit cards are useful if used well, but can be costly and damaging if used badly. The main advantages are that they:

Can offer cheap borrowing or rewards

Let you spread the cost of a purchase

Let you transfer existing credit card debt to 0% (if you get a balance transfer card)

Give you extra protection on purchases

Can boost your credit history when managed well, meaning you're more likely to be accepted for credit in future

The main disadvantages are that they:

Can lead to a build-up of debt if you can't afford to repay what you borrow

Charge interest if you don't clear your full balance each month

Can damage your ability to get credit in future if you miss repayments – this is why we say to always pay at least the minimum repayment each month

### What does APR mean?

APR stands for 'annual percentage rate', and is used by lenders to tell you the cost of borrowing.

Where credit cards are shown as having a 'representative APR', it means only 51% of successful applicants must be given the stated rate. The other 49% could get a different rate (usually higher) – and some people will be rejected altogether.

Lenders must tell you what the APR is before you sign a credit agreement.

If you have a card at a special introductory rate (for example a balance transfer credit card at 0% for 36 months), you won't pay the APR during this time. And if you pay your credit card off in full every month, you won't pay the APR either.

Most credit cards come with a 'variable APR', which means that the interest lenders charge on borrowing (in other words, the outstanding balance on a credit card) can go up or down, depending on market fluctuations. Your lender will have to tell you if it plans to change your credit card APR.
You can also get 'fixed APR' cards, where lenders guarantee they won't raise or lower the rate for a fixed period of time, although these are less common and usually have higher interest rates.

Myth number three, section 75 only applies if you pay the full amount on your credit card. False. This is one of my favourite facts when it comes to credit cards because so many people don't realise that this exists. Section 75 is a protection that you get on purchases that you make on your credit card between £100 and £30,000. So, if something goes wrong with the product or service that you've bought through your credit card, your credit card provider is jointly liable with your retailer to get that money back.

Myth number four, being rejected for a credit card doesn't matter. Unfortunately, it does. Being rejected for any debt can impact your credit score. In the UK, we have three credit rating agencies, Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion. And each of them give you a credit score based on your credit profile.

Myth number five, you should never use your credit card for everyday spending. This one does come down to the individual. I personally do use mine for everyday spending, but I keep a seriously tight check on everything I'm spending on a week-to-week basis really because I use my credit card to make sure that I'm building points or I'm getting the cashback.

So, the big takeaway here: credit cards aren't evil but they're not magic either. Used correctly, they can help you with protection from section 75 and rewards and bonuses, but if used incorrectly can land you in tonnes of debt for decades and interest that you're just spiralling out of control.

You only pay interest on a credit card if you don’t clear your balance in full each month. By paying off your statement balance in full and on time every month, you’ll never pay interest - helping you manage your money effectively and even improving your credit score.

If you’re unsure whether you can pay off your balance in full each month, consider an interest free credit card.

These cards offer an introductory 0% interest period, lasting up to 25

## How to choose the best credit card for you

With so many types of credit card to choose from it can be tricky to decide which might be best for you. Luckily, there are few simple rules you can follow to make sure you pick the right card for your needs:

### Consolidate any debt efficiently

With a balance transfer credit card you can consolidate debts: for a small fee, you transfer all your existing debt onto the new card, which will come with a hefty period of low or even zero interest.

### Build or repair your credit score

If you have a poor credit rating for whatever reason, there are cards that can strengthen your score. With MoneySuperMarket, you can compare credit cards for bad credit, where you could still get a card even with bad credit.

### Seek low interest for everyday spending

Credit cards can be handy for day-to-day spending or spreading out the cost of a larger item - or maybe a big purchase like a holiday. Many cards give you 0% interest on any purchase made within three months or so, saving you the usual cost of borrowing – provided you stick to making your repayments on time.

### Consider if you want rewards

There are many types of credit card that offer rewards on your spending. Frequent flyers can benefit from airline credit cards which give you travel-related rewards. Savvy shoppers can also take advantage of cashback which rewards you when you buy.

## Rewards, cashback, and more credit card benefits

One of the biggest advantages of using a credit card responsibly is the ability to earn rewards and cashback on your everyday spending.

Cashback: Earn a percentage of your purchases back as cash, which can be applied to your balance or redeemed as rewards.

Points and miles: Collect points or travel miles that can be exchanged for flights, hotels, merchandise, or experiences.

Bonus categories: Many cards offer higher rewards for specific spending areas like dining, groceries, or fuel.

Sign-up bonuses & perks: New cardholders often get welcome bonuses, along with extra benefits like travel insurance or purchase protection.

By choosing a credit card that aligns with your lifestyle and spending habits, you can maximise these benefits.

## What are the pros and cons of credit cards?

### Advantages

A 0% purchase credit card is useful for funding big-ticket purchases and affords you time to pay them off without accruing interest

Used responsibly, a credit card can be a good way of improving your credit score

Some cards come with potentially money-saving sweeteners, such as travel perks or cashback

Section 75 applies to credit cards and covers you if a purchase you make is faulty or doesn’t arrive

### Disadvantages

Credit cards are so convenient and easy to use, it can be tempting to overspend and rack up debt

Some card providers charge high fees for missing payments. While others levy annual fees to qualify for rewards

Credit cards usually have variable rates, which means your repayments could rise and make it more costly to service your debt

There are certain credit cards for bad credit which are specifically designed to boost the scores of people who’ve struggled with debt in the past, or people who don’t have much credit history at all (either because they’re young, or because they’ve just moved to the UK).

With some cashback rewards credit cards you’ll earn a higher cashback rate when you shop with certain retailers, or as a welcome bonus.

Cashback can be ‘capped’ – which means you can only earn up to a certain amount each month or year – or ‘uncapped’, meaning there’s no limit on the amount of cashback you could earn.

### Rewards credit cards

With a rewards credit card, customers earn loyalty points on eligible everyday spending.

These points may be part of a retailer’s wider loyalty scheme – Tesco Clubcard points, for instance – or offered by the credit card provider itself.

Points can typically be used to offset the cost of purchases with participating retailers, or exchanged for vouchers and discounts. Some of the best credit card rewards might be redeemable against airline flights, hotels, days out and other experiences, for example. It is important to choose a rewards credit card offering the best deals and offers for you.

The rate at which points are earned depends on the card you choose. Some cards pay points on most everyday spending, while others only offer points when you spend with certain brands.

Depending on the card, you might earn extra points for shopping with certain brands.

## How do reward and cashback credit cards work?

At their core, cashback and reward credit cards work like any other credit card. Customers can use the card to make purchases, provided they stay within their credit limit, and receive a statement every month.

If the balance isn’t cleared in full (usually there is a grace period of 56 days), you’ll be charged interest on your spending.

But cashback and reward credit cards come with a key advantage: you’ll earn back a portion of most spending in the form of loyalty points or cashback which build up over time. The top points credit cards have high levels of cashback or rewards, and many pay higher rates to new customers as a welcome bonus.

Depending on the card you choose, the cumulative points or cash can be used to offset your card balance or spent with one or more partner brands and retailers.

Although you can make cash withdrawals using a cashback or rewards credit card, you won’t earn any points or cashback on these transactions.

In fact, using a credit card to withdraw cash is best avoided altogether as you will typically incur a higher interest rate than applies to purchases. This interest also starts to accrue straight away rather than the typical 56-day grace period.

When choosing a credit card for cashback or rewards don’t forget to look at any monthly or annual fee on the card. It can still be worthwhile having the card for the rewards perks, but you’ll need to weigh up if the benefits and rewards will outweigh any fee.

The Amex Platinum credit card, for example, (not featured in our list above) offers a high level of rewards, including a generous welcome bonus, but with a £650 a year annual fee cardholders need to ensure it makes financial sense for them and that they will make use of the rewards, and other card benefits, on offer.

## Who’s eligible for a cashback or reward credit card?

To be eligible for a cashback or reward credit card, you’ll need to be a UK resident, aged 18 or over.

You’ll also need a strong credit score and no history of bad credit to be accepted for most of these cards. The best rewards credit cards, in particular, tend to require an excellent credit score, and some may need you to have a minimum annual income to be eligible.

Carefully consider where, and on what, you are likely to spend to find the right cashback card for your needs. Several require you to spend a significant amount each month to reap the benefits and/or make specific transactions to gain the top cashback available, for example.

And watch out for any monthly fees which may outweigh any potential cashback or reward benefits.

– Katie Brain, banking insight consultant, Defaqto

Before you apply for a cashback or reward credit card, it’s a good idea to apply for a copy of your credit report.

You can request your report online, free of charge, from any of the UK’s major credit reference agencies: Experian, Equifax and TransUnion.

The report contains an overview of your current borrowing, along with personal details such as your address. Ensuring the report is accurate and up-to-date could boost your credit score, improving your chances of being accepted for a reward and cashback credit card.

Most credit card providers also offer their own eligibility checker tool, which can give you a good idea of how likely you are to be accepted for a card without leaving a mark on your credit file.

## Borrowing limits on a personal loan for bad credit

Borrowing limits are typically lower if you have bad credit, so you might find it difficult to borrow a large amount.

When you apply for a bad credit loan, the lender will run a hard credit check to take an in-depth look at your credit history. To decide how much you can borrow, they’ll also look at:

Your income and everyday spending

How much debt you have

Why you want the loan

Whether you’re securing the loan against an asset.

Use our loan calculator to help you work out how much you might be able to afford to borrow and what your monthly payments could be.

## What counts as a bad credit score?

Each of the three main UK credit reference agencies have a different score for what they consider to be poor or low credit (checked in January 2026).

Experian score range: 0 to 1,250

Equifax score range: 0 to 1,000

TransUnion score range: 0 to 710

## Reasons for a bad credit score

Your credit score could be low if you have:

Failed to stick to a credit agreement

Made late repayments or missed repayments

Been declared bankrupt

Had a CCJ (Country Court Judgment) registered against you

Entered into an Individual Voluntary Arrangement (IVA)

Financial links (such as a joint bank account or mortgage) to someone with poor credit

Multiple credit applications on your credit record over a short space of time. This can suggest to lenders that you’ve having financial difficulties

Never borrowed money before.

## 5 tips to improve your credit score

Here are a few things you could do to boost your credit score and increase your likelihood of being approved for a loan:

Correct any errors on your credit report – you can check your credit report for free. If you spot something wrong, ask the lender or credit reference agency – Experian, Equifax or TransUnion – to correct it.

Register on the electoral roll – loan providers use the electoral register to confirm your identity and address. It’s a key element in building your credit score.

Keep your credit utilisation rate as low as possible – try not to spend more than 30% of your total available credit limit.

Repay existing debts on time – always make your monthly repayments on time. Set up a direct debit to reduce the risk of missing payments.

Make sure your name appears on bills – if you share a home, get your name on one or more of the utility bills. This can help your credit score, as long as you pay them on time.

## Getting a bad credit loan if you’re unemployed

If you’re unemployed and have a bad credit score you might be able to find a lender who’s willing to offer you a loan, but expect to pay a very high interest rate.

Our loan eligibility checker will give you an idea of whether you’ll be accepted for a loan before you apply. It uses a soft search, which doesn’t affect your credit score.

## Alternatives to bad credit loans

Before applying for a bad credit loan in the UK, you might want to consider these options:

A credit-building credit card: typically has a low credit limit. Making your repayments on time and staying within your credit limit could improve your credit score and help you qualify for more flexible options.

An arranged overdraft: several banks offer interest-free overdraft buffers, which let you go overdrawn by a small amount without paying interest.

Borrowing from family or friends: it’s a sensible idea to draw up a loan agreement if you do this, to avoid potential fallouts further down the line.

## What is ‘poor credit’?

If you’ve struggled to keep up with loan, credit card or mortgage repayments in the past, you might be considered to have ‘bad credit.’ This usually translates to a ‘poor’ credit score.

Your credit score can be lacking for several reasons, including:

- Missed or late repayments
- County Court Judgements (CCJs) against you
- previous bankruptcy
- Individual Voluntary Arrangements (IVA)
- applying for credit on several occasions within a short space of time – this can make you appear ‘desperate’ for credit.

Having bad credit means you are less likely to be accepted for a loan.

This is because whenever you apply for credit – whether it’s a mortgage, credit card or overdraft – the lender will check your credit report to find out how reliable you are as a borrower.

## What type of loans can you access with poor credit?

If you have a history of poor credit – or no credit history at all – your choice of loans will be comparatively limited. But you’ll still have a few options to consider:

### Unsecured loans

With an unsecured or ‘personal’ loan, borrowers are not required to use an asset – such as a car or home – as collateral.

If you have a poor credit score, your choice of personal loan deals may be limited, and interest rates will be high. That said, it’s still worth shopping around for this type of loan.

### Secured loan

This type of loan is ‘secured’ against an asset – usually your home. They are sometimes called homeowner loans or second charge mortgages.

If you don’t keep up with your monthly loan repayments, you could lose your home, making this type of borrowing a riskier prospect than its unsecured counterpart.

Lenders may be more likely to offer you credit if the loan can be secured against something tangible like property, however. This usually means interest rates are lower than they would be for equivalent unsecured borrowing.

### Guarantor loan

With a guarantor loan, a trusted friend or family member agrees to take on your debt if you are unable to repay it. Your chosen guarantor will need to have a good credit score. Bear in mind their own ability to borrow in the future is likely to be affected.

Lenders are more likely to offer you credit if they know someone else can step in to make payments in the event you are unable to.

Guarantor loans are unsecured, which means they are not linked to your home or any other asset.

- if you miss a monthly repayment, your credit score go down further
- interest rates are generally higher for borrowers with a poor credit score

- paying your bills on time every month
- applying for new credit no more than once every three months – and ideally leaving six months or more between applications
- keeping your credit utilisation – the percentage of your available credit in use at a given time – to around 30%.
