1️⃣4️⃣ Tower AIRX: 英国本土老牌子，性价比极高，app控制虽然偶有延迟，但胜在便宜耐造。

1️⃣5️⃣ Salter VertiCook: 垂直堆叠的平替版，预算有限但厨房空间也有限的朋友可以闭眼入。

说实话，选机器最忌讳的就是“贪大”。如果你平时就一两个人吃饭，买个10L的大家伙不仅占地儿，清洁起来也费劲。另外，Instant Vortex虽然好用，但新机初期的“塑料味”确实是真实存在的，建议刚到手先空烧两轮。对于咱们在英国的小伙伴来说，如果你家里的烟雾报警器特别敏感，尽量避开那些排气口直冲墙面的老款设计，新款的Ninja和Philips在油烟处理上确实做了不少优化。

总的来说，2026年的选购逻辑就是：大户型看Ninja FlexDrawer，小厨房看Ninja Double Stack，追求口感看Philips Steam，预算有限看Cosori。看准需求再下手，别让它最后在角落里吃灰。

results.summary:
# Ninja CRISPi 4-in-1 vs Salter Crisp & Go: Which portable air fryer is best?

These compact glass air fryers with digital controls are perfect when countertop space is limited, as well for the campervan and caravan crew
...
I for one wouldn’t be without one now, although I was keen to make the transition from a large air fryer to a stacked model to save on some precious worktop space. Going in hard on the space-saving is a new generation of portable air fryers, including the Ninja CRISPi 4-in-1, $180/£160, and Salter Crisp & Go, $99/£90, which have a minimal footprint and are small enough to go in a cupboard. Both models cook in non-toxic glassware, that comes with lids and can be used to store and transport food. I tested them both in my own home, over a period of weeks, to find out which is best.

### Design

The Ninja CRISPi 4-in-1 has a pleasing striking space-saving design and is incredibly well made. Like the slightly smaller Salter, it has a stackable design and two glass cooking containers – 3.8L and 1.4L – which snap onto the PowerPod. Pretty and practical.

While not beautiful, the space-saving, stackable design of the Crisp & Go isn’t offensive either. Build quality is good but not premium like on the Ninja. It comes with 4L and 1.5L glass containers, which both fit the CrisperHub and making ideal for large and single-serving cooking. Both containers come with lids, too, so it’s easy to store what you’ve cooked.

Winner:
...
### Features

The Crisp & Go’s touchscreen panel is responsive and lets you adjust time and temperature, as well as your cooking preset. Choose from Bake, Recrrisp (leftovers), Ultra Crisp (frozen goods) and Air Fry – everything you need and nothing more. The glass design makes it easy to keep an eye on your cooking, too. With its glass containers and PFAS-free coated trays, the Salter Crisp & Go is non-toxic and clean-up is easy too, with handwashing and dishwashing on the menu.

Meanwhile, the CRISPi 4-in-1is perhaps the easiest air fryer to use on the planet. You choose between Keep Warm, ReCrisp, Roast and Air Fry, which all have fixed temperatures that you can’t change, via the mode button. Cook time is set with the timer button. Thanks to the fixed heat protection, you can serve straight from the CRISPi’s non-toxic glass cookware –it’s safe on laminate, butcher block, granite, quartz and marble.

Winner: Draw

### Cooking capability

The Ninja provided results to match its own air fryers that are twice the size and price. I cooked everything from chicken to churros and got excellent results. Using the presets, all I had to do was adjust cooking time which was easy to gauge thanks to the glass cookware.

Similarly, the Salter Crisp & Go provided constantly impressive results, too. The Ultra Crisp preset was particularly good for frozen calamari and kid’s chicken dippers. I appreciated the Recrisp mode to reheat food for my lunch, using the handy 1.5L cooking container. Meats were juicy and fries were fluffy inside and crunchy out.
...
### Overall Winner:
...
Both of these space-saving, portable glass air fryers rival much larger models in terms of cooking results but the Ninja wins due to better design and build quality.

results.title: Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer Air Fryer Review
results.summary:
## Verdict

The Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer Dual Basket Air Fryer is an excellent dual-zone air fryer that provides decently brisk and crispy cooking across a range of foods, plus the added versatility of one big basket when you need it. Its functions are fine for most folks, and the fact that it doesn't need preheating is a huge bonus against more affordable rivals, although some may prefer more functions and a larger basket.

## Pros

- Surprisingly fast and consistent cooking
- Decent overall capacity
- Reasonable functions

## Cons

- Some may need a larger capacity
- Glossy control panel can attract fingerprints

## Key Features

- Review Price: £133.99
- 7.1L capacity: This Philips air fryer has a reasonable capacity in a smaller footprint that's ideal for moderate family cooking loads.
- 6 cooking functions: It also has a good range of food-specific functions for Meat and Chips to Veg, Cake and more.

## Introduction

The Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer Dual Basket Air Fryer takes the powers of a traditional dual-zone air fryer and adds a little more flexibility.

As with dearer rivals such as the Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer Air Fryer 10.4L AF500UK and the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry 10 Litre Air Fryer, this air fryer has the option to remove the divider between the two baskets to create one big one that’s ideal for large batch cooking, or cooking longer food items that won’t fit in the confines of a smaller dual zone basket.

At 7.1 litres in capacity, it is smaller than both Cosori and Ninja’s options, and strips back some of the more advanced functionality (such as top and bottom elements) and features to provide the core experience of a flexible drawer air fryer in a more affordable package.
...
At £133.99 (although often discounted to the sub-£100 mark), it’s cheaper than its rivals, too, and if it can nail the basics, it may well be one of the best air fryers I’ve tested. Let’s take a closer look.

## Design and Features

- Compact profile
- Easy control panel to use
- Reasonable functionality

This Philips FlexDrawer Dual Basket air fryer isn’t what I’d call ‘flashy’ in terms of its looks. It’s more of a generic air fryer, with a matted black plastic chassis and a glossy top panel for controls that can attract fingerprints even with infrequent handling. The actual footprint on a worktop, considering it’s a smaller dual-zone one, isn’t too bad, and it’s quite a compact unit against its larger rivals.

A 7.1 litre capacity is reasonable for moderate levels of family cooking, which can be split into two with the bundled divider to make individual baskets just over 3.5 litres each. There’s enough space in here across the two baskets for fair portions of meat and veg, or you can remove the divider with ease for cooking larger items, such as longer steaks or chips, for instance.
...
The fact that this larger basket is in one piece makes it a little unwieldy to handle and wash up if you’ve got a smaller sink, as I have. It is nonetheless well-built, and the handles on each side are useful. The crisper plates here are of decent quality and easy to take out and put back in when needed, while the silicon divider is convenient for splitting the bigger basket into two separate zones.

As is typical with these cheaper air fryers, this Philips model has functions based on the type of food being cooked, rather than by method. There is a Reheat setting, although the other five functions correspond to Frozen Food, Meat, Poultry, Vegetables, and a Cake setting.

Tapping each function on the glossy control panel atop the unit spits out a preset time and temperature, which can then be adjusted by the temperature and time buttons on either side. It’s easy to do, although the fact that they’re on opposite sides to the way they’re shown on the unit is a small gripe I have. You can also select functions for each basket individually, or as one large instance, plus sync functions and time across both baskets and set a shake reminder.

The top temperature with this air fryer, regardless of function, is 200°C, which is fine, although a little unremarkable if you’re after extra crispy results. For instance, most of Ninja’s air fryers can go up to 240°C on Max Crisp mode for extra-crispy cooking, if you want it.
...
Once you’re done with the fryer basket and crisper plates, they can both be put in the dishwasher. I avoided this in my testing...

I wanted to try cooking chips first to see if they were as good as people claim, but I also wanted to cook a piece of sockeye salmon, so I hit the "fries" button, then adjusted the temperature down from 205 to 200 as a compromise for when the fish would be added half way through the process. I also adjusted the timing up to 22 minutes, but with the intention of checking and stopping the process early if necessary. I found that I could adjust the temperature and time during cooking too, which means you can make changes along the way if your inspections suggest you need them. After 11 minutes it beeped, I turned the chips over, then set the fish on top of some of them to keep it off the metal plate in case it tried to burn onto it, but I needn't have worried as there was no danger of that happening - I'm used to cooking fish on a grill pan on a ring where the heat is transmitted to the fish through contact with the metal, but in the air fryer the heat comes from above and all round, while some conducts through the plate but without risk of anything burning and sticking to it. I opened the basket early a few times to check progress (including before half time) and ended up eating the content two minutes early, but I also opened it early to remove the skin from the side of the fish that had it, this being on the top. I didn't need to turn it over as the underside was fine and it was the newly exposed top surface that wanted most exposure to the heat. I simply picked out the ones that looked as if they were likely to burn and turned them over or ate them at that point.

results.title: 20款扫地机器人“官方测评”结果新鲜出炉！
results.summary:
# 20款扫地机器人“官方测评”结果新鲜出炉！
...
针对消费者普遍关心的问题，北京市消费者协会近期对市场上销售的20款主流扫地机器人产品开展了比较试验。

测试结果显示，受测产品在“单房间覆盖率”“拖地清洁效果”等核心性能上整体表现良好，但不同品牌、不同型号在“矩形框硬地板清洁”“边角清洁”等项目上存在差异。
...
01 核心清洁性能

覆盖率和吸尘能力整体向好，边角清洁能力差异显著

本次试验样品由北京市消费者协会工作人员以普通消费者身份，从电商平台购买，涉及追觅、石头、科沃斯、云鲸、米家、美的、海尔、鲨客等13个品牌的20款产品。价格覆盖1999元至4299元区间。

所有样品均被送至第三方权威检测机构，依据QB/T 4833-2023《家用和类似用途清洁机器人》等标准和测试方法，对单房间覆盖率、矩形框硬地板清洁、边角清洁、拖地清洁效果、自清洁率、防毛发缠绕率及除菌率七个关键项目，进行了科学评测。

在衡量产品全局清扫规划的“单房间覆盖率”项目中，石头、鲨客、科沃斯、MOVA、海尔等品牌表现优异，覆盖率均超过81%，获得五星评价，显示出当前主流产品的路径规划与全屋覆盖能力已较为成熟。

在“矩形框硬地板清洁”的吸尘能力测试中，各产品对大颗粒垃圾的清洁效果普遍良好，但对“小米”等细小颗粒物的清洁效果则存在差异，美的、石头、米家、海尔等品牌表现相对突出。

然而，在精细化清洁场景——“边角清洁”测试上，各产品表现出了显著差异。综合对“标准灰尘”和“小米”颗粒测试的清洁率来看，云鲸、鲨客、萤石、德尔玛、海尔等品牌的部分型号表现相对一般。而在同一测试中，飞利浦、UWANT、MOVA、追觅、米家等品牌则表现更为出色。

02

“拖地自清洁”成标配优势，“防缠绕”功能需关注实测数据

测试发现，拖地清洁、基站自清洁和除菌功能已成为主流产品的标配优势。20款产品的拖地清洁效果评分均达到“良好”级别（70分以上）。在16款宣称具备自清洁功能的产品中，云鲸、美的、海尔、MOVA、米家、追觅、石头等品牌的自清洁率超过95%，获得五星评价。15款具备除菌功能的产品，其除菌率均达到或超过99.99%，满足家庭日常除菌需求。

“防毛发缠绕”是养宠物家庭和长发人群的关注重点。在宣称具备此功能的16款产品中，整体表现较好，但具体效果数据存在差异。报告指出，该功能是一个涉及滚刷、风道、边刷设计的系统工程，消费者在选购时，不应仅凭广告宣传判断，而应关注具体测试数据。

03 消费提示

按需选购，科学使用

基于本次比较试验结果，北京市消费者协会为广大消费者提供了以下选购与使用建议。

1

对照数据，按需购买

数据显示，产品价格与单项性能并非绝对对应。例如，售价4299元的追觅RLS46CE在多项核心指标上均获五星，表现全面。而售价1999元的米家DIO1CN则在多个核心项目上获得四星或五星评价，显示出较高的性价比。消费者可根据房屋面积、地面材质和核心需求（如侧重吸尘、拖地或需防毛发缠绕）进行筛选，重点关注比较试验报告中在相应项目上获得高星级评价的型号。

2

关注续航，提效减负

“续航”包含电池工作时间和水箱（或污水箱）持续时间。建议优先选择电池续航长、水箱容量大或支持自动上下水功能的产品，可避免频繁充电、加水和倒污水，有效减少人工干预频率，真正解放双手。

3

理性看待，定期维护

切勿将“自清洁”功能等同于“完全不用管”。扫地机器人的基站内部、集尘盒、滚刷、边刷等部件仍需使用者定期清理...

results.summary:
# 北京市消协测评20款扫地机器人

2026-03-20 09:36:14来源：中国消费者报
...
边角清洁能力分化明显 防缠绕效果需甄别

■本报记者 万晓东

如今，扫地机器人已成为众多家庭清洁减负的刚需家电，其边角清洁效果、防毛发缠绕能力等备受消费者关注。近日，北京市消费者协会针对市场主流扫地机器人开展专项比较试验，对20款热销产品进行全方位测评。结果显示，受测产品核心基础功能整体达标，单房间覆盖率、拖地清洁等核心性能表现稳定，但边角清洁能力分化明显，防毛发缠绕效果需重点甄别。

核心性能整体向好

边角清洁能力差异大

本次比较试验的20款样品由北京市消协工作人员以普通消费者身份从正规电商平台随机购买，涵盖追觅、石头、科沃斯、云鲸、米家、美的、海尔、鲨客等13个品牌，售价1999元至4299元，兼顾中高端及高性价比机型，贴合主流消费市场选择。所有样品统一送至第三方权威检测机构，严格依据QB/T4833—2023《家用和类似用途清洁机器人》等相关标准，重点围绕单房间覆盖率、矩形框硬地板清洁、边角清洁、拖地清洁效果、自清洁率、防毛发缠绕率及除菌率七大核心项目展开测评。

测试数据表明，当前主流扫地机器人的全屋清扫规划与基础吸尘能力已趋于成熟。在衡量全屋清扫效果的单房间覆盖率项目上，石头、鲨客、科沃斯、MOVA、海尔等品牌样品表现优秀，覆盖率均突破81%，体现出行业在路径规划、智能导航方面的技术升级成果。

在矩形框硬地板清洁测试中，20款样品对大颗粒垃圾的清洁能力均达标，效果相近，但针对细小颗粒物的清洁表现存在差距。其中，美的、石头、米家、海尔等品牌样品在细小颗粒物清洁上表现更为突出，清洁效率更高。

值得关注的是，在日常清洁最易遗漏的边角清洁方面，20款样品表现悬殊。综合标准灰尘、细小颗粒物双重清洁率数据来看，云鲸、鲨客、萤石、德尔玛、海尔等品牌部分样品表现相对一般；飞利浦、UWANT、MOVA、追觅、米家等品牌多款样品，边角精细化清洁能力更强、清洁率更高，能有效覆盖墙角、家具边缘等死角区域。

自清洁除菌成标配

防缠绕功能别轻信

# 北京市消协发布20款扫地机器人比较试验结果：基础功能普遍达标 边角清洁与防缠绕成为选购关键

2026-03-18 19:03:02来源：央广网

央广网北京3月18日消息（记者 庞婷）家中地面清洁如何更省力？扫地机器人的边角清洁能力究竟怎样？养宠物的家庭又该如何选择？针对消费者普遍关心的问题，北京市消费者协会近期对市场上销售的20款主流扫地机器人产品开展了比较试验。测试结果显示，受测产品在“单房间覆盖率”“拖地清洁效果”等核心性能上整体表现良好，但不同品牌、不同型号在“矩形框硬地板清洁”“边角清洁”等项目上存在差异。

覆盖率和吸尘能力整体向好 边角清洁能力差异显著

本次试验样品由北京市消费者协会工作人员以普通消费者身份，从电商平台购买，涉及追觅、石头、科沃斯、云鲸、米家、美的、海尔、鲨客等13个品牌的20款产品。价格覆盖1999元至4299元区间。所有样品均被送至第三方权威检测机构，依据QB/T4833—2023《家用和类似用途清洁机器人》等标准和测试方法，对单房间覆盖率、矩形框硬地板清洁、边角清洁、拖地清洁效果、自清洁率、防毛发缠绕率及除菌率七个关键项目，进行了科学评测。

在衡量产品全局清扫规划的“单房间覆盖率”项目中，石头、鲨客、科沃斯、MOVA、海尔等品牌表现优异，覆盖率均超过81%，获得五星评价，显示出当前主流产品的路径规划与全屋覆盖能力已较为成熟。在“矩形框硬地板清洁”的吸尘能力测试中，各产品对大颗粒垃圾的清洁效果普遍良好，但对“小米”等细小颗粒物的清洁效果则存在差异，美的、石头、米家、海尔等品牌表现相对突出。

然而，在精细化清洁场景——“边角清洁”测试上，各产品表现出显著差异。综合对“标准灰尘”和“小米”颗粒测试的清洁率来看，云鲸、鲨客、萤石、德尔玛、海尔等品牌的部分型号表现相对一般。而在同一测试中，飞利浦、UWANT、MOVA、追觅、米家等品牌则表现更为出色。

“拖地自清洁”成标配优势 “防缠绕”功能需关注实测数据

测试发现，拖地清洁、基站自清洁和除菌功能已成为主流产品的标配优势。20款产品的拖地清洁效果评分均达到“良好”级别（70分以上）。在16款宣称具备自清洁功能的产品中，云鲸、美的、海尔、MOVA、米家、追觅、石头等品牌的自清洁率超过95%，获得五星评价。15款具备除菌功能的产品，其除菌率均达到或超过99.99%，满足家庭日常除菌需求。

“防毛发缠绕”是养宠物家庭和长发人群的关注重点。在宣称具备此功能的16款产品中，整体表现较好，但具体效果数据存在差异。报告指出，该功能是一个涉及滚刷、风道、边刷设计的系统工程，消费者在选购时，不应仅凭广告宣传判断，而应关注具体测试数据。

消费提示

对照数据按需选购，不唯价格论。测试显示，产品售价与单项性能并非完全正相关，高价产品未必各项指标最优，平价产品也有高性价比表现。消费者可结合房屋面积、地面材质，聚焦吸尘、拖地、防缠绕等核心需求筛选。

重点关注续航能力，减少人工干预。建议消费者优先选择电池续航时长充足、清水箱和污水箱容量大，或支持自动上下水功能的机型，避免频繁充电、加水、倾倒污水。

理性看待自清洁功能，坚持定期维护。自清洁功能不等于“零维护”，消费者需定期清理基站内部、集尘盒、滚刷、边刷等核心部件，才能保障机器长期稳定运行，维持最佳清洁效果，守护家庭环境卫生。

选择正规购买渠道，留存维权凭证。消费者应通过品牌官方门店、正规电商平台等渠道购买，妥善保管购买发票、保修卡及相关购买凭证，一旦出现产品质量问题或消费纠纷，可快速享受售后服务，有效维护自身合法权益。

在衡量产品全局清扫规划的“单房间覆盖率”项目中，石头、鲨客、科沃斯、MOVA、海尔等品牌表现优异，覆盖率均超过81%，获得五星评价，显示出当前主流产品的路径规划与全屋覆盖能力已较为成熟。在“矩形框硬地板清洁”的吸尘能力测试中，各产品对大颗粒垃圾的清洁效果普遍良好，但对“小米”等细小颗粒物的清洁效果则存在差异，美的、石头、米家、海尔等品牌表现相对突出。

然而，在精细化清洁场景——“边角清洁”测试上，各产品表现出了显著差异。综合对“标准灰尘”和“小米”颗粒测试的清洁率来看，云鲸、鲨客、萤石、德尔玛、海尔等品牌的部分型号表现相对一般。而在同一测试中，飞利浦、UWANT、MOVA、追觅、米家等品牌则表现更为出色。

“拖地自清洁”成标配优势，“防缠绕”功能需关注实测数据

测试发现，拖地清洁、基站自清洁和除菌功能已成为主流产品的标配优势。20款产品的拖地清洁效果评分均达到“良好”级别（70分以上）。在16款宣称具备自清洁功能的产品中，云鲸、美的、海尔、MOVA、米家、追觅、石头等品牌的自清洁率超过95%，获得五星评价。15款具备除菌功能的产品，其除菌率均达到或超过99.99%，满足家庭日常除菌需求。

“防毛发缠绕”是养宠物家庭和长发人群的关注重点。在宣称具备此功能的16款产品中，整体表现较好，但具体效果数据存在差异。报告指出，该功能是一个涉及滚刷、风道、边刷设计的系统工程，消费者在选购时，不应仅凭广告宣传判断，而应关注具体测试数据。

对照数据，按需购买。数据显示，产品价格与单项性能并非绝对对应。例如，售价4299元的追觅RLS46CE在多项核心指标上均获五星，表现全面。而售价1999元的米家DIO1CN则在多个核心项目上获得四星或五星评价，显示出较高的性价比。消费者可根据房屋面积、地面材质和核心需求（如侧重吸尘、拖地或需防毛发缠绕）进行筛选，重点关注比较试验报告中在相应项目上获得高星级评价的型号。

关注续航，提效减负。“续航”包含电池工作时间和水箱（或污水箱）持续时间。建议优先选择电池续航长、水箱容量大或支持自动上下水功能的产品，可避免频繁充电、加水和倒污水，有效减少人工干预频率，真正解放双手。

results.summary:
# 消协实测20款扫地机器人：边角清洁能力分化明显 防毛发缠绕效果需重点甄别

来源：中国消费者报•中国消费网

发布时间：2026/3/27 17:26:16

如今，扫地机器人已成为众多家庭清洁减负的刚需家电，其边角清洁效果、防毛发缠绕能力等备受消费者关注。近日，北京市消费者协会针对市场主流扫地机器人开展专项比较试验，对20款热销产品进行全方位测评。结果显示，受测产品核心基础功能整体达标，单房间覆盖率、拖地清洁等核心性能表现稳健，但边角清洁能力分化明显，防毛发缠绕效果需重点甄别。

本次比较试验的20款样品由北京市消协工作人员以普通消费者身份，从正规电商平台随机购买，涵盖追觅、石头、科沃斯、云鲸、米家、美的、海尔、鲨客等13个品牌，售价1999元至4299元，兼顾中高端及高性价比机型，贴合主流消费市场选择。所有样品统一送至第三方权威检测机构，严格依据QB/T4833—2023《家用和类似用途清洁机器人》等相关标准，重点围绕单房间覆盖率、矩形框硬地板清洁、边角清洁、拖地清洁效果、自清洁率、防毛发缠绕率及除菌率七大核心项目展开测评。

核心性能整体向好 边角清洁能力差异大

测试数据表明，当前主流扫地机器人的全屋清扫规划与基础吸尘能力已趋于成熟。在衡量全屋清扫效果的单房间覆盖率项目上，石头、鲨客、科沃斯、MOVA、海尔等品牌样品表现优秀，覆盖率均突破81%，体现出行业在路径规划、智能导航方面的技术升级成果。

在矩形框硬地板清洁测试中，20款样品对大颗粒垃圾的清洁能力均达标，效果相近，但针对细小颗粒物的清洁表现存在差距，美的、石头、米家、海尔等品牌样品在细小颗粒物清洁上表现更为突出，清洁效率更高。

值得关注的是，在日常清洁最易遗漏的边角清洁方面，20款样品表现悬殊。综合标准灰尘、细小颗粒物双重清洁率数据来看，云鲸、鲨客、萤石、德尔玛、海尔等品牌部分样品表现相对一般；飞利浦、UWANT、MOVA、追觅、米家等品牌多款样品，边角精细化清洁能力更强、清洁率更高，能有效覆盖墙角、家具边缘等死角区域。

自清洁除菌成标配 防缠绕功能别轻信

随着扫拖一体技术普及，拖地清洁、基站自清洁与除菌功能已成为行业标配。20款受测样品的拖地清洁效果评分均达到70分以上的良好级别，能满足日常拖地需求；16款宣称具备基站自清洁功能的样品里，云鲸、美的、海尔、MOVA、米家、追觅、石头等品牌样品的自清洁率超95%，基站清洁效果出色；15款搭载除菌功能的样品，除菌率均达到或超过99.99%，完全能适配家庭日常除菌保洁需求。

results.summary:
2026年10月09日 星期五

20款扫地机器人测评结果：萤石、海尔等品牌部分样品边角清洁能力相对一般
...
如今，扫地机器人已成为众多家庭清洁减负的刚需家电，其边角清洁效果、防毛发缠绕能力等备受消费者关注。近日，北京市消费者协会针对市场主流扫地机器人开展专项比较试验，对20款热销产品进行全方位测评。结果显示，受测产品核心基础功能整体达标，单房间覆盖率、拖地清洁等核心性能表现稳定，但边角清洁能力分化明显，防毛发缠绕效果需重点甄别。

核心性能整体向好

边角清洁能力差异大

本次比较试验的20款样品由北京市消协工作人员以普通消费者身份从正规电商平台随机购买，涵盖追觅、石头、科沃斯、云鲸、米家、美的、海尔、鲨客等13个品牌，售价1999元至4299元，兼顾中高端及高性价比机型，贴合主流消费市场选择。所有样品统一送至第三方权威检测机构，严格依据QB/T4833—2023《家用和类似用途清洁机器人》等相关标准，重点围绕单房间覆盖率、矩形框硬地板清洁、边角清洁、拖地清洁效果、自清洁率、防毛发缠绕率及除菌率七大核心项目展开测评。

测试数据表明，当前主流扫地机器人的全屋清扫规划与基础吸尘能力已趋于成熟。在衡量全屋清扫效果的单房间覆盖率项目上，石头、鲨客、科沃斯、MOVA、海尔等品牌样品表现优秀，覆盖率均突破81%，体现出行业在路径规划、智能导航方面的技术升级成果。

在矩形框硬地板清洁测试中，20款样品对大颗粒垃圾的清洁能力均达标，效果相近，但针对细小颗粒物的清洁表现存在差距。其中，美的、石头、米家、海尔等品牌样品在细小颗粒物清洁上表现更为突出，清洁效率更高。

值得关注的是，在日常清洁最易遗漏的边角清洁方面，20款样品表现悬殊。综合标准灰尘、细小颗粒物双重清洁率数据来看，云鲸、鲨客、萤石、德尔玛、海尔等品牌部分样品表现相对一般；飞利浦、UWANT、MOVA、追觅、米家等品牌多款样品，边角精细化清洁能力更强、清洁率更高，能有效覆盖墙角、家具边缘等死角区域。

自清洁除菌成标配

防缠绕功能别轻信

随着扫拖一体技术普及，拖地清洁、基站自清洁与除菌功能已成为行业标配。20款样品的拖地清洁效果评分均达到70分以上的良好级别，能满足日常拖地需求；16款宣称具备基站自清洁功能的样品里，云鲸、美的、海尔、MOVA、米家、追觅、石头等品牌样品的自清洁率超95%，基站清洁效果出色；15款搭载除菌功能的样品，除菌率均达到或超过99.99%，能适配家庭日常除菌保洁需求。

results.title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE ou Xiaomi 17T : quel flagship à prix cassé choisir ? — Frandroid
results.summary:
Envie d’un smartphone aux prestations premium sans payer le prix fort ? Les récents Samsung Galaxy S26 FE et Xiaomi 17T sont de parfaits candidats, d’autant plus qu’ils sont en promotion à moins de 650 euros, mais lequel des deux mérite votre argent ?

Pas besoin de dépenser plus de 1 000 euros pour avoir un bon smartphone entre les mains. Pourtant, entre la pénurie de composants et l’envolée des prix de la mémoire RAM, la note grimpe vite sur le très haut de gamme. Heureusement, les marques l’ont bien compris et proposent des alternatives beaucoup plus accessibles. C’est exactement le créneau des séries « FE » de Samsung et « T » de Xiaomi, pensées pour offrir l’essentiel des fleurons sans faire exploser votre budget.

Ils sont justement en promotion et tombent sous la barre des 650 euros : le Samsung Galaxy S26 FE et le Xiaomi 17T offrent des prestations solides et durables, reste à déterminer lequel propose le meilleur rapport qualité-prix.

Sur le plan esthétique, le Galaxy S26 FE reste fidèle aux codes visuels des Galaxy S26 : il opte pour un dos plat en verre, des bords plats avec une armature en aluminium et des bordures très fines autour de l’écran qui est d’ailleurs protégé par un verre Gorilla Glass Victus+. Son design ne manque pas d’attrait et il est complété par une étanchéité certifiée IP68 très rassurante. Le Xiaomi 17T adopte des dimensions plus contenues que son prédécesseur, le Xiaomi 15T, grâce à une dalle qui passe de 6,83 à 6,59 pouces. Ce nouveau format s’avère particulièrement agréable à utiliser au quotidien et profite d’une excellente ergonomie. Les lignes sont épurées, les bords sont plats et les angles sont harmonieusement arrondis. On a même une bonne résistance avec du Gorilla Glass 7i et une certification IP68.

Sur la photo, le Galaxy S26 FE propose une formule polyvalente et très équilibrée grâce à son capteur principal de 50 MP, son ultra-grand-angle de 12 mégapixels et son téléobjectif de 8 mégapixels avec stabilisation optique. Dans l’ensemble, il capture de belles photos, quelles que soient les conditions d’éclairage. Les photos sont particulièrement convaincantes de nuit, sauf avec l’ultra grand-angle. Mention spéciale pour le téléobjectif. De son côté, le Xiaomi 17T fait appel à Leica pour son module photo. Il est composé d’un capteur grand-angle de 50 mégapixels, d’un ultra-grand-angle de 12 mégapixels ainsi que d’un téléobjectif périscopique x5 de 50 mégapixels qui est d’ailleurs l’atout majeur du 17T.

Des écrans bien équipés avec une interface fluide

Sur la partie affichage, les deux constructeurs déploient de très belles dalles AMOLED à 120 Hz. Xiaomi marque des points avec une luminosité maximale en pic impressionnante (jusqu’à 3 500 nits) et une définition 1,5 K très fine (2756 x 1268 pixels), garantissant une lisibilité parfaite en plein soleil. L’écran du S26 FE n’en démérite pas pour autant : il offre une bonne luminosité, une excellente fidélité des couleurs et des angles de vision très larges.

Sur l’expérience logicielle, si les deux utilisent Android, on a la surcouche HyperOS sur le Xiaomi 17T contre One UI sur le téléphone de la firme sud-coréenne. Le S26 FE offre une interface complète, comprenant de nombreuses fonctions dopées à l’IA. Que ce soit pour améliorer la productivité ou faciliter la retouche et l’enrichissement des photos, la panoplie est complète et efficace. Pour rassurer ceux qui gardent longtemps leur smartphone, le constructeur garantit 7 ans de mises à jour majeures d’Android et de correctifs de sécurité. L’interface de Xiaomi est aussi fluide aux animations retravaillées et aux icônes épurées. La « Hyper Island » imite la Dynamic Island d’Apple pour afficher des informations et HyperAI est plutôt complet. On regrette tout de même la présence de pourriciels. Enfin, les 5 ans de mises à jour du système d’exploitation sont bienvenus.

Performants, mais l’un est plus endurant

Les deux smartphones sont suffisamment performants pour la plupart des usages.

...
隨著人工智慧（AI）應用快速擴張，全球資料中心對記憶體的需求持續攀升，市場開始出現 RAM 供應吃緊的跡象。據《Android Authority》報導，AI 產業正以前所未有的速度採購 RAM，已逐步擠壓消費性電子產品可用的記憶體供應，並可能在 2026 年反映在智慧型手機售價上，尤其是價格敏感度較高的入門與中階 Android 手機。

報導指出，雖然多數手機品牌在 2025 年仍自行吸收部分成本壓力，但市場已傳出部分品牌下一代機種可能因 RAM 短缺而調漲售價，漲幅甚至上看 10%。在此背景下，若消費者原本就有換機需求，提前在價格尚未明顯反映前入手，反而更具成本效益。《Android Authority》整理出目前幾款價格親民、且仍具競爭力的 Android 手機，供消費者參考。

### Google Pixel 9a：七年更新成最大賣點

Pixel 9a 被外媒評為目前最均衡的平價 Android 手機之一。該機在相機表現、日常效能、電池續航與 AI 功能之間取得良好平衡，最大優勢在於 Google 承諾提供長達七年的系統與安全更新，在 Android 陣營中相當罕見。

儘管 Google 預計於 2026 年推出 Pixel 10a，但外媒認為，新機價格可能因 RAM 成本上升而突破 550 美元，相較之下，現行售價約 499 美元、且經常搭配促銷的 Pixel 9a，仍是更具吸引力的選擇。

### OnePlus 13R：效能取向的平價選項

對於重視效能表現的使用者而言，OnePlus 13R 是另一個值得考慮的機型。該機主打高效能處理器與大容量記憶體配置，整體流暢度與反應速度表現突出，也具備不錯的螢幕品質與快充能力。

不過，OnePlus 13R 在相機與長期軟體更新承諾方面，仍不及 Pixel 系列，但若以效能與使用手感為主要考量，仍具一定競爭力。

### 三星 Galaxy A16 5G：品牌穩定度取勝

Galaxy A16 5G 屬於三星在入門 5G 市場的主力機型之一，提供基本但穩定的效能表現，搭配三星熟悉的 One UI 操作介面與完整通路支援，對於預算有限、但偏好大廠品牌與售後服務的消費者而言，是相對安全的選擇。

雖然硬體規格不特別突出，但在價格、品牌信任度與系統支援之間取得平衡，仍具一定市場吸引力。

### Nothing Phone 3a：設計導向的差異化路線

Nothing Phone 3a 最大特色在於透明機身與 Glyph 燈效設計，主打視覺辨識度與個人風格。外媒指出，該機較適合重視外型設計、而非單純追求性價比的族群。

在規格與價格競爭力方面，Nothing Phone 3a 並非最突出的選項，但獨特設計仍讓它在同價位產品中保有差異化定位。

### Moto G Stylus（2025）：少見內建手寫筆

Motorola Moto G Stylus（2025）則以內建手寫筆作為主要賣點，適合經常記筆記、標註文件或進行簡單繪圖的使用者。整體硬體規格屬於中規中矩，但手寫筆功能在平價機市場中相對少見，形成特定族群的吸引力。

要注意的是，報導中所提及的機款有部分未在台灣市場上市。

RAM 供應持續吃緊，價格較低的入門與中階手機，反而可能因成本轉嫁而面臨較明顯的漲價壓力。相較之下，已上市、且定價尚未反映成本變化的機型，短期內更具吸引力。在 AI 與資料中心需求持續推升記憶體使用量的趨勢下，消費性電子產品的成本結構正悄然改變。外媒建議，有換機計畫的消費者，應密切關注 RAM 供應與價格變化，避免在價格調整後才進場。

1. 預算範圍：高階、旗艦、還是 CP 值機種？
首先買手機最重要的，是要先確認自己的預算範圍！像是「旗艦手機」適合追求頂規體驗的使用者，預算大約在新台幣2萬5千元以上～8萬元不等；而預算有限、追求高CP值機種的人，則可以選擇千元或1萬元出頭的「入門/中階手機」，兼顧價格與實用性。

### 中階手機（約 NT$11,000–$19,000）：流暢日常體驗、長電池續航、效能均衡且價格合理。

### 入門手機（約 NT$10,000以下）：實用基本功能，適合日常使用和輕量需求。

2. 使用需求：拍照、遊戲、日常用還是長輩機？
你的手機主要使用需求是什麼：愛打高效能遊戲？重度拍照玩家？長時間追劇？長輩日常使用？
由於不同族群適合的手機都不同，建議先釐清有無特殊需求和優先排序，就能幫助你選出適合自己的機型。

3. 系統偏好：iOS 還是 Android？
目前主要有兩大手機系統：iOS 、 Android ，你習慣哪個操作介面、生態系很重要，也會連帶影響到其他3C裝置的相連性使用，所以這也是一項選擇關鍵點！

results.summary:
# 詢價排行榜：一萬多元就能買到旗艦體驗？高 CP 值手機正在成為換機新主流

Billy 2026-06-13 11:36 | 手機綜合區

手機市場近期出現一個相當有趣的現象，過去總是由高階旗艦主導的詢價排行榜，如今開始被價格更親民、規格卻不俗的機種挑戰。尤其隨著新機推出速度加快，加上消費者換機觀念逐漸改變，「夠用、划算、規格均衡」開始成為不少人的選購重點。從本週排行榜來看，過去由三星 Ultra 系列與 iPhone 長期盤據前段班的局面，首次被高 CP 值機種打破，也反映出台灣消費者對價格敏感度持續提高。

廣告

## 小米 17T Pro 強勢登頂
本週最大焦點無疑是 小米 17T Pro。該機以 2,941 次詢價直接衝上排行榜冠軍，不僅超越近幾週穩坐第一的三星旗艦，更成為近期少數能夠打破 Samsung 與 Apple 壟斷榜首的機型。從排行榜走勢來看，小米 17T Pro 上週才剛進榜便拿下第七名，本週隨即衝上第一，成長幅度相當驚人。對於不少消費者而言，17,900 元的價格帶剛好介於中高階與旗艦之間，再加上性能與規格配置具備競爭力，因此迅速吸引市場關注。此外，小米 15T Pro 也持續留在榜內，以 981 次詢價排名第九，顯示 Xiaomi 在高 CP 值市場的布局開始發揮效果。

## Ultra 旗艦仍穩守高階市場
雖然榜首被小米拿下，但高階旗艦市場仍然由 Samsung 主導。Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 本週以 2,289 次詢價排名第二，持續維持強勁熱度。即便已上市一段時間，仍穩定占據排行榜前段位置，顯示 Ultra 系列依然是許多高階用戶換機時的首選。而前代旗艦 Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra 則以 1,442 次詢價排名第七。近期可以發現，S25 Ultra 雖然不再與新機正面競爭榜首，但憑藉價格優勢，始終維持穩定詢價量，也讓「買新旗艦」與「撿便宜舊旗艦」兩種需求同時存在。

## iPhone 維持穩定人氣
Apple 陣營本週排名變化不大，整體表現依舊穩定。Apple iPhone 17 以 1,942 次詢價排名第三，繼續扮演系列中的主力產品；而 Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max 與 Apple iPhone 17 Pro 則分別位居第五與第六名。此外，定位較入門的 Apple iPhone 17e 也持續進榜。從目前榜單觀察，Apple 雖然沒有出現像 Xiaomi 那樣的爆發性成長，但整體產品線仍維持相當穩定的市場關注度。

## 中階市場依舊是兵家必爭之地
除了旗艦機之外，中階市場依舊相當熱鬧。Samsung Galaxy A57 5G 本週以 1,917 次詢價排名第四，甚至緊咬 iPhone 17，持續展現驚人的競爭力。從近兩個月的榜單來看，A57 5G 已經從中階黑馬逐漸變成固定班底。另外，Samsung Galaxy A56 5G 也以 1,113 次詢價排名第八。兩款 A 系列同時進榜，也反映出台灣消費者對萬元級手機的需求依舊相當穩定。

手机中国 【原创】 作者：毛志超 2026-06-03 10:04
...
【CNMO科技消息】近日，安兔兔发布5月安卓手机性价比榜单。安兔兔强调，性价比榜机型基于性能榜和京东自营价，跑分数量不够的机型自然没有；部分机型在京东自营下架了，自然也没有；出现在榜单上的配置，为该机型综合性能之后性价比最高的配置；没出现在榜单上，不代表机型性价比不高；售价来自出数据时的当天京东自营售价，并且未计算国补。

真我GT8

0-999元

第一名为OPPO K12s 5G，参考售价为934元，搭载骁龙6 Gen 4、7000mAh电池。第二名为REDMI Note 15，参考售价806元，搭载骁龙6 Gen 3、5800mAh电池。

安兔兔：这个价位段的核心变化是处理器从骁龙695、天玑7025-Ultra升级到了骁龙6 Gen 4、骁龙6 Gen 3，中低端芯片的性能提升让百元机的跑分水涨船高，性价比值自然也跟着上去。

1000-1999元

第一名为REDMI Turbo 5 Max，参考售价1699元，搭载天玑9500s、9000mAh电池。第二名为一加Ace 5至尊版，参考售价1784元，搭载天玑9400+、6700mAh电池。

安兔兔：这个价位段的性价比值从4月的1200-1300元区间飙升到了1500-1600元区间，涨幅超过20%，是目前性价比最高的价位段了。

2000-2999元

第一名为真我GT8，参考售价2203元，搭载骁龙8至尊版、7000mAh电池。第二名为真我Neo8，参考售价2199元，搭载骁龙8 Gen 5、8000mAh电池。

安兔兔：真我GT8的2K 144Hz屏幕和5000万像素长焦镜头是同价位独一无二的配置；真我Neo8的8000mAh电池、165Hz三星屏也竞争力十足。

3000-3999元

第一名为一加15T，参考售价3069元，搭载第五代骁龙8至尊版、7500mAh电池。第二名为真我GT8 Pro，参考售价3292元，搭载第五代骁龙8至尊版、7000mAh电池。

安兔兔：一加15T是小屏旗舰的唯一选择，194g重量和6.32英寸屏幕在同价位独树一帜；真我GT8 Pro的2亿像素长焦镜头和2K屏幕体验极佳。

4000元以上

第一名为iQOO 15 Ultra，参考售价4349元，搭载第五代骁龙8至尊版、7400mAh电池。第二名为红魔11 Pro，参考售价4498元，搭载第五代骁龙8至尊版、8000mAh电池。

安兔兔：iQOO 15 Ultra是iQOO首款Ultra机型，4349元的售价配合400万的跑分，是整个安卓阵营目前跑分最高的机型之一；红魔11 Pro延续游戏手机定位，内置风扇散热，4498元的售价在这个价位段排第二。

随着居民健康饮水意识不断提升，净水器在现代家庭中应用越来越广泛，不同户型、不同用水需求的家庭，适配的净水产品也有所区别。市面上家用净水产品主要分为 RO 反渗透与超滤两大类型，也是家庭选购最常纠结的品类。其中 RO 反渗透过滤精度可达 0.0001 微米，能够有效滤除水中水垢、重金属、余氯以及各类细菌病毒，过滤后的水体可直接饮用，机器需要通电运行并产生少量废水，更适配北方高硬度水质、老旧小区以及有宝宝的母婴家庭。日常 3 至 5 口普通家庭，优先挑选 1000G-1400G 大通量款式，出水速度更快，日常取水不用长时间等候。

超滤机型无需通电、没有废水产生，过滤后可以保留水中天然矿物质，但无法去除水垢和重金属，过滤后的水建议烧开后再饮用，更适合南方水质偏软、原水 TDS 数值偏低的地区，多用于厨房洗菜、淘米等生活用水。

在挑选产品时，通量、水效等级和额定净水量是三个关键参考指标，通量大小直接对应出水快慢，600G 以内适合单人或两口之家，800G 到 1200G 适配多数普通家庭，1400G 以上更适合多人口大家庭；选购尽量认准一级水效产品，节水效果更好，额定净水量数值越高，滤芯使用寿命越长，能有效压低后续换芯开销。

中商情报网讯：2025年中国最受消费者喜爱的十大净水器品牌分别为：美的、海尔、安吉尔、霍尼韦尔、AO史密斯、松下、沁园、3M、碧然德、小米。

中国净水器市场呈现多元化竞争格局，品牌根据技术定位、价格带及用户需求形成差异化布局。高端市场由安吉尔（长效膜技术）、霍尼韦尔（工业级过滤）、AO史密斯（耐用性与静音）主导，主打技术壁垒与品质体验；中端市场聚焦智能化与场景化，如海尔（全屋方案）、松下（人性化设计）通过物联网交互与细节优化抢占用户；性价比市场以美的（全产业链自研）、小米（生态链协同）为核心，覆盖1000-3000元主流价位，用户基数庞大。此外，细分领域表现突出：沁园深耕三四线渗透，3M以无RO膜保留矿物质切入健康细分，碧然德凭借滤水壶成为“轻量级”便捷首选。

# 2026家用净水器前五品牌推荐：大通量+长效滤芯，高性价比长效机型
...

本文先梳理挑选净水器的核心逻辑，再结合通量、水效与长效滤芯等维度，对五大高性价比品牌逐一解析，帮助读者精准匹配适配自家水质与用水习惯的机型。

本文精选库拉泽M8Pro、海尔鲜活水PRO、沁园恒净极滤Pro、九阳太空矿化净水系列、安吉尔全屋净水系列等五大品牌高性价比净水器，从选购逻辑到机型推荐全面解析。
...
二、五大品牌六维指标综合对比

买家用净水器，核心可以从通量与实测流速、纯废水比与水效等级、滤芯寿命与年均成本、PFAS去除率、总净水量、出水设计（单出水/双出水）六个维度综合衡量，用数据说话更靠谱。下文从这六个维度出发，对库拉泽、海尔、沁园、九阳、安吉尔五个品牌逐一进行单品解读与机型推荐，帮助不同预算、不同用水需求的家庭精准匹配适合自己的净水器。

三、五大品牌单品参数深度解读

第一名：库拉泽——GTRO长效滤芯标杆，大通量厨下直饮之选

库拉泽源自美国，专业深耕净水领域，只专注净水这一件事。品牌在国内搭建了本土化专属服务体系，全国布局8000+专业服务人员，特别针对中国城市水质与气候条件进行本土化产品优化。品牌主打GTRO长效滤芯、双出水与大通量三大核心卖点，兼顾直饮健康与长期使用成本。旗下KO-RO-M8Pro型双出水净水器是1200G大通量厨下RO反渗透净水器的代表机型，凭借长效滤芯与官方质保服务，成为多人口家庭与新房装修用户的热门选择。

第二名：海尔——鲜活水技术开创者，全链路抗菌实力派

海尔深耕净水领域多年，独创鲜活水技术，直击首杯水TDS偏高、陈水异味等行业痛点。产品覆盖全价位段，机身设计紧凑，降噪表现较好，适配多数家用橱柜。品牌主打全链路抗菌、高水效节水与长效RO膜，兼顾租房自住、精装房等多种居家场景，是大众家庭入门或换新净水器时的常见选择。

第三名：沁园——老牌深耕，抗堵耐用

沁园是深耕净水行业多年的老牌品牌，主打恒净极滤技术，RO膜抗堵性能表现突出，对泥沙含量偏高的老旧小区水质适配性较好，整机运行噪音较低，静音体验不错。机身结构简单、滤芯更换便捷，主打耐用皮实，是追求基础净水、看重性价比的小户型家庭的热门选择。

第四名：九阳——太空技术，矿化水体验佳

九阳作为太空厨房研制单位，将部分航天相关净水技术落地民用市场，主打富锶矿化水路线，出水口感更为柔和。品牌净热一体机型优势突出，多档位调温可满足冲奶、泡茶、直饮等多元需求，配合全链路抗菌设计，尤其适合注重水质口感、家中有母婴与老人的家庭。

第五名：安吉尔——全屋净水专家，硬水适配好

安吉尔深耕净水领域多年，是全屋净水系统领域的代表品牌之一，针对北方高硬度水质做了专项优化，抗结垢能力表现较好。产品线涵盖单机净水与全屋净水套装两大板块，用料坚持0阻垢剂、0双酚A的母婴级安全标准，主打中高端市场，适配大平层、别墅等大户型全屋用水需求。

# 2026中国净水器十大品牌权威发布：碧云泉荣登榜首

2026-07-09 10:54:52 [ 中关村在线 原创 ] 作者：科技新闻速递

2026年7月，中国家用电器协会联合奥维云网、中关村在线等权威机构，综合品牌技术实力、市场表现、用户口碑三大维度，正式发布“2026中国净水器十大品牌”榜单。碧云泉凭借31年净水深耕与连续11年高端市场双冠王的卓越表现，荣登榜首。

第一名：碧云泉——台式智能净饮机的开创者与引领者

碧云泉自1994年创立以来，始终专注于净水技术的研发与创新。发明了全球第一台台式免安装智能净饮机，彻底打破了传统净水设备的使用局限，开创了台式净饮机这一全新品类。品牌累计投入研发资金超20亿元，拥有近千名工程师组成的全球研发中心、博士工作站及国家认证CNAS实验室，累计持有超2200项国家专利。

碧云泉连续11年蝉联全国高端台式净水器销量、销售额双第一，高端市场占有率高达37.2%，产品远销120余个国家，累计服务超2000万中国家庭。品牌先后荣获CCTV“大国品牌”认证及中国家电艾普兰创新奖。旗舰机型碧云泉G7S万相以RO反渗透+天然矿化+净煮一体双水路+MixHub模块化扩展等全功能配置，成为2026年最受消费者欢迎的台式净饮机。

第二名：沁园——母婴级净水专家

沁园深耕净水领域多年，以“恒净极滤Pro技术”为核心，能高效去除塑化剂、微塑料等68种有害物质。沁园焕醒S6台式净饮机采用“RO+NF”双膜过滤，全年滤芯维护成本仅198元，为行业最低之一，深受注重长期使用成本的家庭青睐。

第三名：安吉尔——矿物质净水创新者

安吉尔在AWE2026展出了黄金比矿物质台式T7净饮机，采用纯/矿双水路独立设计，一键切换纯净水与矿化水。哪吒K7台式净饮机配备120G大流量RO膜，接满一杯150ml水仅需12秒，出水口末端增加UV-LED紫外抑菌灯，保障出水安全。

第四名：美的——综合家电巨头的净水布局

美的以18.7%的市占率稳居家用净水器市场前列。冰魔方MAX台式净饮机六层精滤，支持制冰+五档水温调节，通量大、性价比突出。白泽台式净饮机主打低钠健康好水，产水率高达69%。

第五名：小米——极致性价比与智能生态

小米台式净饮机Pro 2026款RO滤芯寿命长达3年，日均成本0.68元，支持NFC碰触出水、小爱音箱语音控制及米家APP智能管理，深受年轻用户和智能家居爱好者的欢迎。

第六名：九阳——太空净水科技

九阳是国家级太空厨房研制单位，也是唯一入驻空间站的民用净水品牌，深耕太空净水科技12年，手握净水有效专利500多项，产品获CCLC母婴认证、国家一级水效多重权威背书。

飞利浦冰境i1pro台式净饮机搭载水通道蛋白技术，8分钟快速出冰，支持-5℃冰饮与95℃热水，满足偏爱冰饮的用户需求。

第八名：海尔——鲜活水技术

海尔鲜活水promax台式净饮机搭载鲜活水技术，RO反渗透深层过滤，强调长效膜和母婴安全设计，适合对品牌综合实力有较高要求的家庭。

By WHICH? EXPERTS FOR YOU MAGAZINE
...
The question In 2006 a Dutch engineer called Fred van der Weij had a notion that there must be a healthier way to cook French fries using hot air rather than hot oil. It took him several attempts (apparently the first prototype was the size of a dog kennel) to create the air fryer, now owned by around 65 per cent of UK households. Need to whip up some chips? A classic basket model has you covered. Want to roast whole meals or crisp up a pizza? Go with an oven air fryer. Cooking main dishes and sides together? Choose a dual-zone model. So, which should you buy?

The basics Which? has tested more than 70 air fryers, from a £35 Total Chef model to a £270 Ninja one.

The method Which? whizzes assessed how well each air fryer cooked chips, chicken drumsticks and baguettes. They noted their speed, energy usage and ease of cleaning. The quickest air fryers took just 20 minutes to cook four portions of chips, without preheating, while the slowest took over 45 minutes.

The thing to remember Which? buys the products its tests, which means no relying on freebies, and no biased results.

Even though Ninja was very much the brand to bring the whole ‘FlexDrawer’ concept to the public eye, the Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer Air Fryer shows that there’s more than enough room for another brand to take a crack at the same design, particularly from a more budget-friendly standpoint. If you’ve been tempted by Ninja’s FlexDrawer air fryer but have a limited amount of cash to work with, then Philips’ alternative is your best bet.

If you’re unfamiliar, the FlexDrawer design means that this Philips air fryer can provide an entire 7.1L compartment for cooking larger meals, but when you want to have two different modes running simultaneously, maybe to cater for a main protein and a side dish, then you can have two compartments set up in mere moments. It’s a great idea that works well here, especially if you’re part of a medium-sized household and you need a good amount of versatility to help you cook a breadth of meals.

Arguably the most important factor however is that regardless of whether you’re using a single drawer or two, the air fryer itself does an excellent job with pretty much any type food you throw at it. With a few rashers of bacon, the Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer made them all nice and crispy in just five minutes, while a more involved meal including chicken breasts in one drawer and arancini plus croquettes in the other, came out juicy and flavoursome.

It was a similar situation when cooking vegetables exclusively. We ran a test including hasselback potatoes, a handful of carrots and broccoli too. This healthy medley of ingredients was subjected to a 200°C cook over 15 minutes, and it all came out tasting great. If you’re looking for an excuse to whip up healthier meals in a pinch then this is easy means of doing so.

As great as this Philips air fryer is, it’s hard to shake the feeling that the FlexDrawer system is at its best when there’s a larger capacity involved. Ninja’s FlexDrawer air fryer carries a much larger 10.4L capacity which makes it far better suited for larger households, so if you do have quite a decent number of people to cook for then you may want to pick up Ninja’s offering instead, there’s a lot to like here.

A good-quality air fryer is an investment, so check its programs, ease of cleaning and temperature/time range before you buy. There’s no need for the lower temperatures and long durations (usually up to 12 hours) for dehydrating fruit and fermenting yoghurt if you’ll mostly be using it for air frying, for example. Similarly, if you’re a keen cook, look for one with plenty of space – a small air fryer may soon limit your horizons.

For those with a dishwasher, check that drawers and crisping plates are safe to clean this way, while if you’re cleaning by hand, robust nonstick coatings will make degreasing easier.
...
Yes, both because you need a lower amount of oil – a tablespoon should be enough to coat a 500g batch of chipped potato, while other foods require no oil at all – but also because the way food is “fried” is different.
...
Linger on social media long enough and you’ll find worries about air fryer toxicity. It’s usually centred on plastic parts growing hot (which, as it’s limited to the exterior of air fryers, rather than the parts that come into contact with food, shouldn’t present a problem) and nonstick coatings containing Pfas/PFOA.

Most manufacturers have phased out PFOA (since 2013, all Teflon products have been PFOA-free), while potential deterioration of nonstick (which may use Pfas as this is a term for a large group of chemicals) tends to happen at temperatures of 260C and above. Most air fryers have a limit of 200C, with the top temperatures on others 240C.

If you’re concerned about the safety of nonstick, choose an air fryer with a ceramic-coated pan and plates, or clean yours carefully:
...
Another concern linked to air fryers is about cooking starchy food, which produces acrylamide (a potential carcinogen).
...
Cooking oil at high temperatures can also produce potentially harmful compounds. Air fryers don’t use much oil, but if you’re concerned about this, choose an oil with a high smoke point (the temperature at which oil starts to smoke and break down), such as vegetable, peanut, sunflower or rapeseed.
...
Air fryers have gained a reputation for being economical, and while this is true for the most part, it won’t always be the case. For small amounts of food, air fryers use less energy, heating up quickly and only circulating hot air within a small space. An example, a A+-rated 72-litre oven might use 1.395kWh to cook a roast chicken over 90 minutes, while an air fryer could do the same job in less than an hour and use only 0.782kWh – almost half the energy and cost.

# The Ninja Crispi is Tech Advisor’s Best New Air Fryer of 2025-26

News

Dec 24, 2025

## A modular air fryer for the way people live today

A few years ago, air fryers were a rarity. Now they’re the norm. Most of us do at least some of our daily cooking in an air fryer. They’re faster, easier to use and, crucially right now, cheaper to cook in than an oven. Each iteration brings new innovations that take us further from the original black countertop box with a pull-out drawer.

There are so many types of air fryer that we now have dedicated round-ups for the best air fryer of all types, the best dual-drawer air fryer, the best air fryer oven – and we even have a Ninja-specific round-up.

But this year’s winner was easy to choose. It’s a complete reinvention of what an air fryer should be able to do, and how you can use and store it. We’ve also awarded a runner-up prize.

## Best New Air Fryer of the Year – Winner:
...
Like last year’s winner, Ninja’s Double Stack XL, we expect this model to be much copied over the next few months. But as yet, the Crispi is unique.

Why? It’s a modular air fryer that gives you much more freedom over how you use and store it. It’s the first ever alternative to the monolithic countertop appliances that currently dominate both retailers and homes across the world. Ordinarily, if you buy an air fryer, you’ll stick it on your counter and that’s what you’ll be looking at every time you enter your kitchen.

Not so the Crispi, which you can store in pieces in a cupboard. It’s made up of a heating element, two countertop-safe glass dishes (3.8-litre/4-quart and 1.4-litre/6-cup) and two lids that fit the dishes.

Cooking is simple: attach the cooking head to one of two glass cooking dishes. When your food is ready, you can bring the dish to the table and serve it straight from there. Have leftovers? Pop one of the supplied lids on the dish and stick it in the fridge. Plus, as all parts except for the cooking head are dishwasher-safe and there are no non-stick surfaces to protect, you really can just throw everything in the dishwasher at the end.

The Crispi isn’t just innovative for its own sake – it works for the way people live now. Not everyone has a large, dedicated space for cooking equipment. Plus, more and more people have housemates, and communal appliances can be a source of contention: who made the mess and who’s going to clean it up? A cooker you can pack up and store means you can choose whether to share.

It does have limitations. There are only four cooking modes – bake, air fry, recrisp, and max crisp – and its lower capacity means that sometimes the oven will be a better option. But the Ninja Crispi is genuinely innovative and the perfect air fryer for cooking for one.
...
## Best New Air Fryer of the Year – Runner-Up: Tefal Easy Fry Dual Air Fryer and Grill

Rebecca Shepherd / Foundry

A dual-drawer air fryer would be our recommendation for most families. Two drawers mean you can cook an entire meal in your air fryer, without having to switch on the oven at all. But Tefal’s Easy Fry Dual Air Fryer and Grill has some extra features that elevate it beyond rivals of the same type.

Tefal has made the decision to split the drawer sizes asymmetrically. Most dual-drawer models have cooking areas of the same size, which can mean there’s not enough space for mains for four people – and wasted space for a side. This model’s cooking zones have a 5.2L and 3.2L capacity, giving you space in the larger drawer for an entire chicken.

The other function that sets it apart from rivals is that the larger cooking zone can grill, providing a healthier way to cook bacon, and bringing more taste to chicken and fish. Grilling is one of eight pre-set cooking programmes, others of which include fries, chicken, vegetables, fish, dessert and dehydrate. That means it’s versatile and the learning curve to using it is gentle.

Not only is it sturdily made but we were impressed by its power. It’s a 2700W appliance. Although this means that, on paper, it could cost more to run, what we actually found when we tested it was that it cooks food extremely quickly, so it’s efficient to use.

## What’s New from IFA 2026?

A ton of robot vacuums were announced at IFA 2026, from vacuums that will be available this year to concept vacuums like the iRobot Duo. They're from brands all over the world and will be available here in the United States, as FCC approval was given before the new ban was announced. Here are a few that caught my eye that I plan to test in my home this fall:

Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV for $1,200: Dyson's newest version of the Spot+Scrub is already here, but this time adds a UV light to help its AI spot stains. I'm excited to see how this one compares to my favorite Shark vacuum with similar features. It's out now, and keep an eye out for my review.

Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry for $700: Dyson also added a more budget-friendly robot vacuums to its lineup, and the R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry will both vacuum and mop for well under $1,000. It has triangular cleaning pads for getting into corners, as well as Dyson’s new Twin-capture system that promises more efficient debris removal.

Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry for $550: This is another, cheaper option from Dyson and is a true robot vacuum, with no mopping technology. Dyson says it's engineered for deep cleaning across hard floors and carpets with intelligent floor and dust sensing, and it has Dyson’s Twin-capture technology.

Eufy Omni E35 for $1,300: This robot vacuum is interesting to me as a parent, since it promises baby-grade cleaning with its Asthma & Allergy Friendly certification and TÜV-certified testing that shows 99.99 percent bacteria elimination. It also has 35,000PA suction and an updated self-cleaning roller mop, and washes with 140 degree Fahrenheit hot water (at the start, and the water does cool off as the robot moves through your home). It also adds stain detection and removal, which I'm looking forward to testing.

Roborock Saros 20 Flow for $1,700: While I'm currently testing the base Saros 20, the Saros 20 Flow is coming out next with roller mop technology instead of spinning mops, a retractable LiDAR turret (while the base Saros 20 doesn't have LiDAR), and 36,000 Pa of suction.

Roborock Qrevo 3 Edge Pro for $1,500: The Qrevo line continues to grow this year, and now the Qrevo 3 Edge Pro is added to the mix. (It'll be called the Saros 20 Neo in other countries.) It promises impressive threshold crossing with the ability to get itself over 3.46-inch obstacles thanks to the AdaptiLift Chassis 3.0, warm water mopping, and an impressive 36,000 Pa of suction. It'll also have the FlexiArm technology I've liked on other Qrevo models like the Qrevo 2 Pro. It's available now.

## Other Robot Vacuums We’ve Tested

3i G10+ Robot Vacuum for $250: If you want a super-affordable vacuum with no docking station but still great specs, this is the one to get. It has shockingly powerful suction for the price point (18,000 Pa) and a 1-liter dustbin built into the vacuum. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So was particularly impressed with its navigation and how well it did at edge cleaning. It’s a mop, too, which is even more impressive at this price point. If you’re looking for cheap but still great, it doesn’t get better than this. However, it's currently only available used, and I'm keeping an eye out to see if it comes back in stock or is getting discontinued.

Eufy S2 for $1,600: This robot vacuum has an intense-looking base station. However, I was disappointed it missed both the fridge and bookshelf Cheerios in my corner test, giving it only a one out of three. Both cherry stains were scrubbed away, but the floor near where the stains were felt sticky all over even with the stains ostensibly wiped away. It’s especially a bummer given the price point.

Best on a Budget

If you’re looking for vacuuming and mopping but don’t want to pay close to or beyond a four-figure sum, this is the vacuum to choose. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So previously recommended Eufy’s older X10 Pro Omni as a great robot vacuum without spending too much, and Eufy released the Eufy Omni C28 at the end of February with a similar set of features and price point. The Omni C28 comes with nearly double the suction power of the older model, a self-cleaning roller mop instead of mop pads, and retractable detangling brushes.

It does a solid job mopping and vacuuming, but it has a shorter battery life, leaving it at only 37 percent after completing the four-room main floor of my house. This is a bit of a bummer, since this affordable vacuum can do multi-floor mapping. While it can store enough maps to clean all three levels of my home, it doesn’t have the battery life to do so. But it does charge fairly quickly, and I was able to still clean all three floors of my house in a single day—I just had to let it recharge a little at the base first. It went back up to 57 percent battery life after just 20 minutes in its docking station.

With my corner Cheerio test, this vacuum also got two out of three Cheerios, but it missed the trickier fridge-corner Cheerio. This is the hardest spot to get into, so I’m not surprised, but it does mean you’ll have to check those corners more with this vacuum. The cherry juice spill test also showed similar results: the first spot it reached was cleaned completely, while the second spot, which had more time to dry, still had some sticky residue left behind.

Overall, though, it’s a good vacuum for the price, especially since it packs multi-floor mapping, the capability to mop and vacuum, and good results all around for a vacuum that’s already usually on sale for around $500.

## Roborock Saros 20

The Saros 20 is the successor to the hugely popular Saros 10R. It keeps everything we loved about that older version, but introduces a couple of significant updates that help level it up. The main one is an upgraded 'AdaptiLift' system. This is essentially all the tech surrounding the little feet that can lift the robot up away from the ground.

The Saros 20 will be able to climb over even taller room thresholds than its predecessor. I saw it tackle a massive double step in the Roborock demo area at CES, and while it did come down with a bit of a bump, it was still impressive to behold. If you have high room thresholds in your home, this improvement could make all the difference.

There's a second trick related to the AdaptiLift feature: it can now hold the robot at a range of preset heights. This means it can hover at just the right height over a thick carpet or rug, cleaning it efficiently without getting stuck.
...

## Dreame X60

Dreame is another of my favorite robot vacuum brands, consistently delivering reliable, effective, and user-friendly bots. Like Roborock, it was showcasing a few different models at CES, but the one that'll be most practical for most people is the X60.

The key update is that this bot has been on a diet – it's significantly shallower than its predecessor, and in fact might well be the thinnest robot vacuum on the market right now (it's about the same height as the Saros 20 above).

If you have a low-slung sofa, chances are this bot will now be able to venture under it and clear away all the dust bunnies that have built up since you last bothered to lift the sofa out and clean beneath it.
...
Another headline update here is that the cleaning station now uses hotter water to wash the mop pads. Much hotter. Boiling, in fact. The idea is that it'll cut right through any grease and grime so your mop pads are like-new by the time the robovac ventures out on another cleaning spree.

As with the Roborock Saros 20, there's also a retractable LiDAR puck (helping to keep the overall height down), and mini legs to vault it over tall room thresholds.

Both Roborock and Dreame are widely available in various countries, including the US, UK, and Australia, but not everything arrives at the same time.

Picking a programming laptop isn’t about throwing maximum budget at specs – it’s about matching hardware to your actual workflow. ### CPU and RAM: The Compilation Engine

Your CPU determines how fast code compiles, tests run, and how many parallel tasks you can run. For most programming work, multi-core processors matter more than raw clock speed because compilers, transpilers, and test runners use parallel processing. AMD Ryzen 7 and Intel Core i7 chips with 6+ cores handle most modern dev workflows smoothly.

RAM is where most developers underestimate their needs. 16GB is the minimum for comfortable multitasking with an IDE, browser, and a database. # Experts from Which? tested more than 700 mattresses - these are the best three, including a budget buy for just £139!
...
The basics Since 2012, Which? experts have tested more than 700 mattresses, with the cheapest costing £99 from Ikea and the most expensive being £3,870 from Vispring.

The method To assess the mattresses, testers used several objective methods, such as simulating a decade’s worth of sleep by rolling barrels, thousands of times, over them and then measuring any sag. They were placed in humidity chambers to test their breathability in hot conditions and warmth in cold ones. Which? also tested if each mattress was simple to carry, gauged whether it was easy to roll over on and measured the position of a sleeper’s spine to check it provided adequate support. (Softness and firmness are not viewed as a positive or negative, because comfort is a personal preference – instead testers gave a measurement of 1 to 10 for firm to soft.)

The thing to remember Unlike other product experts, Which? buys the items before testing them. That means there’s no relying on freebies and no biased results.

See the full range of expert-recommended mattresses at which.co.uk/mattress

## How we test mattresses

Telegraph Recommended’s experts have ranked and reviewed 45 mattresses to find the best on the market. They sleep on each one in their own homes for at least one month, scoring against the following criteria:

- Comfort: Our testers judge whether they sleep well on the mattress, wake each morning free from aches and pains and if it is breathable.
- Support: They assess whether the mattress keeps their spine correctly aligned and if it takes pressure off their hips and shoulders.
- Motion isolation: They fill a glass with water and place it in the middle of the mattress. In a mattress with minimal motion transfer, you should be able to apply pressure around the glass without any liquid spilling over the sides.
- Edge support: Testers sit on the side of the mattress and assess how much it dips beneath their weight and if it rebounds quickly when they move.
- Convenience and design: Finally, they consider delivery, the length of any sleep trials and the warranty. Here we assess care instructions and manoeuvrability, too.

Freelance writer and reviewer Kirsty Bosley tested the Emma Hybrid Airgrid.

The Simba Hybrid Pro has been tested twice, a thorough approach befitting a Best Buy. First, Recommended reviews editor Simon Lewis tried it. Then, commissioning editor Hannah Mendelsohn has shared her experience sleeping on it for four years. We have compiled all their findings to reach our final verdict.

## Why you can trust Telegraph Recommended

Our thorough, real-world tests will always help you find the best sleep product. No manufacturer ever sees Telegraph Recommended reviews before publication and we don’t accept payment in exchange for favourable reviews, nor do we allow brands to pay for placement in our articles.

All reviews are based on independent expert opinion and our hands-on testing.
...
## Comfort

Simba: 9/10

Emma: 8/10

Far from being objective, most brands rate firmness using their own subjective scales. So, while the Simba Hybrid Pro is described as medium-firm, and the Emma Original Elite Mattress as medium-soft, it’s hard to know what that means in reality.

Mendelsohn says of her Simba mattress: “It’s certainly softer than the pocket sprung mattress I owned before. It’s comfortable in most sleep positions [...] and takes the pressure off my joints, too, so it’s always a pleasure to get into bed.”

Although Emma touts the Original Elite Mattress as medium-soft, our tester Bosley found it firmer than expected. “It takes some adjusting to if you’re used to a soft mattress,” she says. “It took me about a week, but now I love it.”

Breathability is important too. The Emma mattress’ memory foam features internal pockets throughout to boost the flow of air. Bosley found this effective at regulating her body temperature, but slow to warm up on particularly cold nights.

In contrast, Simba relies on a thin layer of moisture-wicking wool and graphite-infused memory foam to conduct excess heat away from the body. Lewis and Mendelsohn both praised this, but which of the two mattresses feels more comfortable for you in this regard is ultimately a matter of personal preference.

Winner: Simba

## Edge support

Simba: 10/10
...
Good edge support means you can comfortably sit or sleep on the side of the mattress without rolling off. It’s especially important for older people or anyone who struggles with mobility and would benefit from stable support getting into and out of bed.

So, when a mattress has bad edge support, you’ll know. But, good edge support is rarely remarkable. It just feels solid and sturdy. Both the Emma Original Elite and Simba Hybrid Pro are consistently supportive right the way across.

Mendelsohn says: “I often sleep on the edge of the Simba Hybrid Pro with no bother at all. It dips slightly when I sit on it, but I’d expect that from something containing foam, and it always bounces back up.”

results.title: We asked 815 readers for the best place to buy a mattress – and no, it isn’t John Lewis
results.summary:
Each mattress has a star rating out of five, determined by a score out of 100, which takes into account the metrics mentioned above.

Your average Telegraph reader knows what they like and sticks to it, so it’s no surprise that 74 per cent of our respondents would stay loyal to the same brand if they had to buy another mattress. Their rationale was proven quality, comfort and durability. If our readers had to switch, their most frequently mentioned second-choice brands are Simba, Dreams, Emma and Silentnight.

Drilling down into the feedback, Bensons for Beds was the favourite for value for money and shopping experience. Sealy, known for its orthopaedic mattresses, had the highest score for its reputation, while Simba stood out for the weight distribution, stability and noise reduction of its products.

None of the brands achieved standout scores for sustainability, hypoallergenic properties, ease of rotation or pain reduction.

Readers’ Choice

## Simba

Simba makes our current best mattress for most people, the Simba Hybrid Pro, so it’s no surprise that it comes out on top in our survey, with the highest scores for stability and weight distribution (both 5/5). It has strong appeal and an excellent reputation, too.

It is one of the original bed-in-a-box brands, and readers praised its online shopping experience. There’s also a generous extended sleep trial: 200 nights to get used to the feel of your new mattress. But if you’d rather try before you buy, its mattresses are available in select John Lewis, Bensons for Beds and Barker & Stonehouse showrooms.

Its mattresses come with a 10-year guarantee, which is longer than Bensons or John Lewis, but the same as Tempur and Hypnos. You’ll need to rotate your mattress regularly to maintain the guarantee, but be prepared to enlist a friend or two to help you. Ease of rotation was one of the few categories where Simba achieved a less than favourable rating: just 3.5/5.

Best Value Mattress Retailer

## Bensons for Beds

Bensons for Beds is the only retailer to meet the threshold for a Best Value badge, scoring a perfect five. If you’re working with a tight budget, the site has a dedicated section for mattresses under £500. Then, use the sliding scale to set your budget down to exact pounds and pence, so you’re never tempted by a mattress outside of your price point.

It received mixed reviews for the mattresses themselves; airflow, pain reduction and maintenance were all average while weight distribution and stability were good. But given its extensive range, this is hardly surprising. It stocks most mattress types, many leading brands and its own ranges.

In any case, it was also the only brand to receive top marks for its shopping experience. Every Bensons showroom has something called Sleeppro. Essentially, it’s a smart mattress cover that takes your temperature, measures your weight and determines your pressure points to identify the most suitable mattresses for you to try.

If you’re buying a mattress for the first time in years, and you’re feeling overwhelmed by choice, all this makes Bensons a good place to start.

## Tempur

Tempur secured two of the highest scores for brand reputation and consumer appeal (4.5/5). In fact, looking through the comments, some of you thought that Tempur invented memory foam, but that was NASA using viscoelastic foams to absorb motion from aircraft cushions. Tempur took that material and refined it for the bedroom.

And it works. Tempur achieved some of the highest scores for product satisfaction, with stand-out ratings for weight distribution, noise reduction and stability. Tempur’s mattresses are notoriously heavy and hard to manoeuvre though, which lowered its score.

The most common complaint about Tempur mattresses is the cost. You should expect to spend at least £1,000 to secure even a single mattress. Consequently, its value for money score is just 3.5/5, lower than any other brand in our top five.

## Sealy

Sealy is one of the more premium brands on our survey, with the highest score for brand reputation. It’s close behind Simba for consumer appeal too and they are tied for value for money. For much of the pre-purchase experience, the two brands are neck and neck.

The gap only starts to appear post-purchase. According to Telegraph readers, Sealy mattresses are heavy and difficult to rotate, scoring just 2.5/5 in that category. On the plus side, such solid construction might account for its high scores for weight distribution and stability. Sealy gets a silver medal for ease of cleaning too, scoring above the average but pipped to the post by Simba.

The fiber scientists in the Good Housekeeping Institute Textiles Lab have tested over 250 mattress models through hands-on analysis and with the help of at-home consumer testers. We've also surveyed more than 10,000 mattress owners to get data on the beds they purchased for themselves.

All in all, we've reviewed responses to more than 180,000 questions before making our recommendations. We continue to update this page as we receive new insights and as new mattresses are tested by our experts. Here's how we evaluate each model:

✔️ Expert research: We start by reviewing materials, specifications, added features and any noteworthy claims. We also vet the brands to check for common complaints and make sure they're trustworthy. Sometimes mattress brands do a great job of marketing to get on your radar, but we've eliminated ones with red flags for quality or customer service.

✔️ Hands-on analysis: Next, product experts and consumer testers experience the mattresses firsthand for setting up and sleep testing. We ask for feedback after several weeks, then again after extended periods to see how the mattresses hold up over time. We also survey our larger tester panel for additional feedback on the mattresses they own.

✔️ Ordering & delivery: Users tell us whether the mattress was easy to order and if it arrived quickly. If there were any problems during the delivery process, we get intel on how (and if) those issues were resolved by the brand.
...
✔️ Setup: Our reviewers weigh in on the setup process, regardless of whether it was DIY or via delivery service. They also rate whether the mattress quickly took shape after arrival.
...
Testers share feedback on how comfortable and supportive the mattress felt, including opinions after sleeping on the mattress right away and after a longer adjustment period.

✔️ Firmness level: Each tester gives a perceived firmness rating, which is important because sometimes the brand's claimed rating doesn't match what users feel during real use.
...
Users tell us about whether the edges of the mattress sink in under their weight or hold up to pressure.
...
✔️ Temperature regulation: Regardless of cooling claims, we ask reviewers to rate how comfortable their body temperature remained while sleeping on the mattress.
...
Our survey respondents weigh in on whether the mattress seemed to affect their sleep quality (good or bad!) and whether or not they woke up feeling sore. They also give the mattress an overall satisfaction rating and have the opportunity to compare the model to previous beds they've slept on.

✔️ Additional feedback: In addition to scored questions, our testers have the opportunity to specify likes, dislikes and additional comments to help us get a full picture of their testing experience.

## How to shop for a mattress

There isn't one model that's best for everyone, so it's important to think about your personal needs when shopping for a mattress. Here's what to consider before you buy:
...
✔️ Sleep position: The goal is to keep your spine in neutral alignment, so factoring in how you sleep can help narrow down your search. Stomach sleepers need a firm mattress, side sleepers should opt for a softer surface to avoid stress on the pressure points like your shoulders, hips and knees, and back sleepers (and anyone who changes positions) would fall somewhere in between at a medium firmness.

✔️ Body type: Heavy people need a firmer bed for support, while lightweight frames are better suited with a softer mattress. Take into account both your weight and sleep position when deciding on the right firmness level.

✔️ Back pain: If you suffer from lower or upper back pain, look for a pressure-relieving mattress with all foam or a hybrid of foam and coils. Medical experts also advise looking for medium firmness for a balance of cushioning and support.
...
✔️ Temperature: Hot sleepers or anyone dealing with night sweats would benefit from a mattress with cooling properties. Memory foam tends to sleep hot, so look for a mattress with coils for airflow or cooling technology like copper particles, gel or phase change technology that's added to the foam.

✔️ Trial period: It's difficult to know whether a mattress is a good fit without actually sleeping on it. Fortunately, most mattress companies offer an any-reason return period for at least 100 nights. Before you buy, check whether there are any hidden return fees and how you go about making the return to avoid any headaches later on.

### What is the best rated mattress on the market?

The Simba Hybrid mattress is the best-rated mattress by Ideal Home's review team. We test a lot of mattresses, yet this crowdpleaser has retained its crown as our #1 rated mattress for the past five years.

This mattress is a great all-rounder that offers a good level of cushioning and support. Simba's delivery and customer service are first-rate, and at £899 for a double, it's good value for money.

### How much should I spend on a mattress?

I recommend spending between £800 and £1200 on a mattress. You can get an okay mattress for around the £500 mark if your budget won't stretch that far, but they tend to feel softer and don't offer as much support. That likely means they'll lack durability too.

A budget of £800-plus will get you a decent memory foam or memory foam hybrid mattress. A pocket spring mattress made with natural materials will tend to cost a little more, usually from £1200 upwards.

It's worth considering that a good mattress should last you between seven and ten years. That means you could be sleeping on it for up to 3650 nights. Spending £1200 works out at an investment of 32 pence per day on a good night's sleep.

### Is an expensive mattress worth it?

Having tested multiple mattresses at all ends of the price scale, in my opinion, yes, an expensive mattress is worth it, within reason. The mattresses we've tested between £1500-£3000 have offered more layers and used better quality materials than more affordable options. You do get what you pay for.

Plus, you don't necessarily need to pay full price. Our mattress deals page keeps track of all the latest discounts, with savings particularly common during the January sales and the month of Black Friday in November. Time your purchase during a sale and you could save a significant amount.

### Which is the best mattress brand?

After four years of testing mattresses, Simba, Silentnight, and Sleepeezee are my top recommendations if you're looking for an affordable mattress. Sealy is a great choice for a firmer mattress, and Tempur offers some of the best memory foam mattresses if you want a mattress that really cushions the joints. If breathability and a cooler sleep are important to you, opt for a natural mattress; Hypnos, Harrison Spinks, Button & Sprung, and naturalmat are all great brands to consider.

## Best mattresses by sleep position

Sleeping position can, and should, be one factor you consider when choosing your mattress. Whereas back and stomach sleepers need a firmer mattress, side sleepers and combo sleepers should look for a softer mattress.

## Best mattresses by sleep concern

In a perfect world, everyone would wake up feeling limber and fresh. Yet, 1 in 10 people wake up with some sort of ache or pain. If that's you, then choose your mattress based on the firmness and type that will best support your sleep.

## How to choose the right mattress

There is a lot to consider when choosing a mattress.

“First and foremost is your sleeping position and firmness,” says Derek Hales, the founder and editor-in-chief of NapLab.com, a sleep-testing platform.

Hales says that the majority of sleepers prefer a medium to medium-firm mattress, but your sleeping position is what tips the scale. Side sleepers typically prefer a softer mattress, whereas back and stomach sleepers do better with a firmer mattress.

Other important factors to consider include:

- Mattress type (memory foam, innerspring or hybrid)
- Mattress size
- Mattress thickness
- Price, based on your budget

“Company policies are important as well,” says Hales. “Having a trial period and a warranty you feel comfortable with is important.” Online mattress brands commonly offer free shipping and free returns, so you won’t feel like you’re locked into a mattress once you buy it.

## What mattress size do I need?

The size of the mattress you need depends on the number of people (and pets) sleeping in the bed, your size, the size of your room, and how much you like to spread out.

“Full mattresses are a good choice for single adults who like to spread out more,” says Hales. “Whereas a Queen mattress is the right pick for couples and/or those who sleep with pets. Co-sleeping with kids is also possible with a Queen, but it is certainly more difficult compared to co-sleeping in a King.”

The general assistants are powerful, but they weren’t built with keyword clustering and content calendars in mind. The marketing-focused tools fill that gap, and several have evolved far beyond simple copy generators. The best ones now run a loop from research to brief to draft to optimization without you having to stitch three different apps together.

### Jasper
...
enterprise content teams, branded marketing at volume

Used by Akbank, Adidas, and Cushman & Wakefield. Jasper’s Brand Voice feature is genuinely impressive. It reads your existing content, infers your tone and style, and then maintains that consistency across everything it generates.

Over 50 templates cover the standard marketing content types. The Kanban-style campaign manager is a genuine productivity gain for teams. It’s expensive, and it’s ultimately GPT under the hood, but the workflow layer earns its price for content operations at scale.
...
### Surfer SEO
...
SEO-first content teams, anyone writing for organic search traffic

Surfer remains the gold standard for on-page SEO writing support. In 2026, its most important evolution is its move toward Answer Engine Optimization (AEO). It now helps structure content to appear in AI-generated search overviews, not just traditional Google results. For any team whose traffic depends on organic search, Surfer isn’t optional; it’s infrastructure.

The points-based scoring system makes optimization accessible even for writers who have never opened a keyword research tool.

### Copy.ai
...
high-volume short-form copy, automated marketing workflows

The king of short-form. Perfect for high-volume social media posts, ad copy, and Workflows that automate your entire content calendar.

Copy.ai’s Workflows feature has become one of its main attractions. You can automate entire content pipelines, from prospect research to personalized outreach to social posts, without writing a line of code. For a marketing team running dozens of campaigns simultaneously, the time savings are substantial. It won’t produce your brand’s most nuanced long-form content, but that was never the point.

## Creative and fiction writing

This is where the tool market gets genuinely interesting and where most general-purpose assistants fall flat. Writing fiction isn’t about producing grammatically correct text. It’s about sustaining tension, building character interiority, managing pacing across hundreds of pages, and generating descriptive language that doesn’t read like a product listing. The creative writing tools understand this distinction in a way that ChatGPT, for all its versatility, simply doesn’t.

### Sudowrite
...
fiction writers of any level, from hobbyists to publishing professionals

The most purpose-built fiction tool in the market. Sudowrite’s Story Engine can outline entire novels, and its Describe function generates sensory scene descriptions across specific senses. You can ask it to render a scene through smell alone or through sound. Its Canvas feature provides a bird’s-eye view of your manuscript structure. The Write button, which generates the next 300 words when you’re stuck, is simple in concept and wildly effective in practice.
...
If you’ve been circling that novel for three years, this is the tool that might finally tip you into actually writing it.

### editGPT
...
writers who want proofreading without personality erasure

The distinction that makes editGPT worth knowing: most AI editing tools optimize for correctness, and in doing so, they sand away everything that makes your voice your voice. editGPT uses a Track Changes-style interface so you can review every proposed alteration and keep or reject it.

It catches what needs catching, such as structural issues, clarity problems, and clunky phrasing, without turning a writer’s distinctive style into sanitized AI-speak. For writers who care deeply about their voice, that restraint is the whole product.

### Scrivener
...
novelists and long-form writers who already live in Scrivener

Scrivener is, first and foremost, a manuscript management tool; it has been so for two decades. Its 2026 AI plugins don’t try to write your book for you. Instead, they help you maintain internal consistency across a 90,000-word manuscript: tracking character descriptions, flagging plot-hole candidates, checking that your fictional world’s rules haven’t contradicted themselves.

For serious long-form writers, this is an organizational layer that no general-purpose chatbot can replicate.

## Academic and professional tools

The stakes change when writing has real-world consequences, when a citation matters legally, when a wrong fact in a report affects a business decision, and when your institution can penalize you for plagiarism. The academic and professional category is defined by a single obsession: accuracy. These tools sacrifice some of the creative fluency of the general assistants in exchange for verifiability.

这份报告不打算给你一份面面俱到的清单，只挑十款我真正长期用下来、能说清楚它到底解决了什么问题的工具，按使用场景整理，附上我个人的真实感受，供你按需取用。

### 一、写作与通用对话

#### Claude：写作这件事上，它依然是最顺手的

如果你让我只留一款通用AI，我大概率会选Claude。不是因为它在每个维度都最强，而是它最懂"写作"这件事。

我的用法很固定：把过去写过的几篇文章丢给它当风格样本，它就能稳定地模仿我的语气和结构。这一点在别的工具上我也试过，效果差不少。它还有一个我特别依赖的能力，对指令的遵循度。我有一套校对提示词，让它帮我校对整篇文章，同时保留原意和语调，Claude基本能做到改错不改味。同样的提示词放到别处，经常是改着改着就把我的意思带偏了。

适合谁：日常写作、文案、需要稳定风格输出的文字工作者。
...
### 七、我的选型建议

十款工具测下来，我最大的感受是：没有一款工具能包打天下，选型的关键是你当下最痛的问题是什么。

如果你只是个人提效，写作、搜索、做PPT、读资料，那Claude、Perplexity、Gamma、NotebookLM这几款按需组合就够了，成本低、上手快。

ChatGPT 是一款終極多用途基礎平台，最適合尋求多功能助手的一般知識工作者與開發者，能處理從複雜程式編碼到快速腦力激盪的各種需求。

ChatGPT 採用最新版本的 GPT-4o 架構驅動，具備極為直覺的聊天介面，已成為業界標準。其核心優勢在於多模態能力；使用者可上傳資料試算表以即時進行資料分析、在行動裝置上以語音指令操作，或生成程式碼片段。它能快速解決「空白頁症候群」的日常困擾，即時生成結構化的大綱、電子郵件與報告。

然而，其真正的企業價值存在於原生網頁介面之外。與其強迫員工保持 ChatGPT 分頁開啟並反覆複製貼上文字，具有前瞻思維的企業會利用 OpenAI 強大的 API。透過開放 API 與 webhook 將 ChatGPT 的底層模型直接整合到像 Lark 這樣的全方位平台中，團隊可以觸發 GPT-4 來摘要團隊聊天內容、翻譯文件，或自動建立核准流程，讓所有企業資料集中且安全。

優點：

- 無與倫比的多模態能力（語音、視覺與進階資料分析）。

- 龐大的外掛與 API 生態系統，便於企業整合。

- 高度適應的推理能力，能應對複雜問題解決。

缺點：

- 可能會出現偶發性「幻覺」（自信地陳述錯誤事實）。

- 網頁介面在長且雜亂的聊天記錄下，可能很快變得混亂。

價格：

- 免費方案：包含對 GPT-4o 功能的有限存取以及基本資料分析。

- Plus 方案：每位使用者每月 20 美元，提供優先存取權與更高的訊息上限。

- 團隊方案：每位使用者每月起價 30 美元，具備加強的工作區管理功能。

results.summary:
### Why I love it

### Pricing
...
Unlike Claude—where you have to ask the AI to make changes—Gemini lets you format, reorganize, and rewrite directly in the document.

It’s the first AI editor that feels like a real workspace, not just a chat box pretending to be one.

When I’m working on SEO-heavy pieces, I switch to Deep Research.

It scans top results, summarizes the trends, and gives me a full report—turning what used to be hours of SERP-hopping and a 27-tab research spiral into a five-minute read.

And for long-form projects, Gems and Instructions make life easier.

I use Gems like mini Custom GPTs. Each one remembers a client’s tone or structure guide, so I don’t have to retype it every time.

To use the Gem, I open it and type in the chat as I normally would when prompting.

I also keep a few custom instructions—little reminders about tone and formatting—saved inside Gemini, so when I start a new draft, it already sounds like me.

I saw Gael Breton (Authority Hacker) call Gemini’s Canvas ‘the most complete AI writing environment yet’—and I couldn’t agree more.

It’s the first time I’ve felt I could finish an entire draft without leaving the app—and honestly, I didn’t miss my usual chaos of 20+ open tabs.
...
Gemini has a free student plan and a general one, with paid plans starting from $6/month for Pro and $20/month for Plus, which is the better option.

## 4. Surfer

I used to write for algorithms instead of people, buried in keyword spreadsheets and SEO guesswork.

Surfer changed that.

It helps me write for search intent, not just search engines, and shows what AI models actually surface.
...
Surfer takes the guesswork out of SEO writing. It feels like having an optimization coach sitting next to you, showing you what to add, cut, or reword in real time.

Here’s are the AI features that stand out most for me:

- Content Score for live SEO performance tracking.
- Auto-Optimize for instant NLP term enrichment.
- Surfy AI Assistant for in-editor rewrites and SEO tweaks.

The Content Score is my north star.

I used to overcomplicate SEO with a dozen tabs open—now I just watch my Content Score climb. It updates as I write, showing exactly how close my draft is to what’s already ranking.

It’s surprisingly accurate too—Surfer’s data shows Content Score has a stronger correlation with rankings than backlinks.

When I’m tightening up an article, Auto-Optimize does the heavy lifting.

It analyzes my draft against the SERPs, adds missing keywords and context, and boosts the score instantly.

Then there’s Surfy, the built-in AI writing assistant.

I use it to rephrase clunky sentences, add examples, or back up claims with data—right inside the Content Editor.

Just highlight text and type “/AskSurfy.” It’s like ChatGPT for SEO writers, but smarter about context.

And when I’m done?

One click to auto-insert internal links and another to export to WordPress.

It’s the kind of end-to-end workflow that makes Surfer feel more like a production hub than a tool.

It’s everything I need to go from keyword to optimized article in one workspace, and that’s why it’s at the top of my personal AI-writing toolbox.
...
The Essential plan starts at $79/month (annual billing), with Scale and Enterprise tiers unlocking AI visibility tracking, more credits, and collaboration tools to generate content.

There’s no free plan, but you get a 7-day money-back guarantee—enough time to see how much easier SEO writing can be.

## 5. Lex

I’ve tried more AI writing software than I can count, and most still feel like chatbots cosplaying as content creation tools.

Lex isn’t one of them. It was clearly built by someone who understands the writing process and stared down a few thousand drafts.

It’s clean, fast, and smart enough to help without getting in your way, whether you’re writing fiction or marketing copy.
...
Lex feels like Google Docs or Microsoft Word got a quiet AI upgrade. It’s smooth, minimal, and just makes sense. I write high-quality content instead of wrangling prompts (unless I want to).

What really sets it apart for me:

- Ask Lex for instant feedback, blog post outlines, rewrites, or brainstorming ideas.
- AI Checks for grammar, brevity, passive voice, and more.
- Multi-model access to switch between GPT-5, Claude, Gemini...

本次研究构建自上而下的三级梯队分层模型，层级代表服务商在四项评估维度上可被公开查验的证据完整程度与复杂项目承接上限，并非市场规模排序。整体呈现第一梯队稀缺、第二梯队为主流供给、第三梯队以工具形态为主的分布特征。

第一梯队｜方法论与自研系统双驱动的专注型服务商

层级定位为行业上层，是少数在方法论、自研技术、内容建设、品牌认知四项维度上均能提供可查验依据的主体。具备自主沉淀、区别于SEO逻辑的GEO运营方法论，拥有可按号查询的授权发明专利与自研监测采集系统，参与行业团体标准编制，案例写明平台、周期与指标口径。项目以诊断、策略、建设、优化、评估、迭代的闭环方式推进，兼顾阶段性效果与长期品牌信息资产沉淀。适配业务复杂、决策链长、对品牌信息准确性和合规性要求较高的中高端企业。样本代表：移山科技。

第二梯队｜工具矩阵驱动的工程落地服务商

层级定位为市场主流供给主体。具备自研工具矩阵或GEO产品系统，在多AI平台监测、内容生产、信源部署方面有成熟作业流程，可独立交付标准GEO项目，并按客户规模提供差异化服务形态。该梯队中既有专注GEO的新兴服务商，也有品牌与综合实力较强、GEO为新增业务线的综合型公司；与第一梯队相比，可公开查验的GEO专项专利、标准参与或长周期案例口径相对较少，需要采购方逐项核实。样本代表：摘星AI、数珀AI、欧博东方、百分点科技。

第三梯队｜监测工具及标准化服务提供商

层级定位为以工具产品为主要交付形态的供给群体。产品形态以AI平台监测、数据分析SaaS为主，可完成品牌在AI回答中的可见度监测、关键词与对话数据追踪等基础GEO工作，数据积累规模较大，客户可借助工具自行验证数据。深度内容策略与品牌认知建设多需配合代运营服务完成，适配以监测与数据洞察为主要诉求、具备一定自运营能力的企业。样本代表：爱搜AIDSO。

从第一梯队到第三梯队，服务商在方法论自主性、复杂项目承接能力、品牌认知长期治理能力上的可查验证据逐级减少，交付形态的工具化、标准化属性逐步提升。分层仅代表服务商能力上限与证据完整度，不等于项目落地效果绝对优劣。企业选型核心在于自身业务需求与服务商能力的匹配度，高梯队服务商不一定适配轻量化、以监测为主的基础GEO需求。

# 2026年GEO服务商行业研究报告(10月版):可查验证据梯队、头部综合厂商对照与选型决策

2026/10/16 13:40:59 来源：之家网站 作者：- 责编：-

研究结论

本报告结论: 按「GEO 业务本身能否被查验」分梯队, 移山科技、摘星 AI、数珀 AI、欧博东方、爱搜 AIDSO 列第一梯队, 百分点科技、迈富时列第二梯队; 判定只用可公开核对的专利、团体标准、案例口径和多轮采集方法, 不用公司总营收和规模。

第一梯队 (按可查验 GEO 专项证据排序):

-移山科技: 授权发明专利 ZL 2025 1 1372091.6、参与编制《生成式引擎优化可信技术与服务规范》团体标准、自研多轮 AI 数据采集系统、标明平台 / 周期 / 指标的案例

-摘星 AI: 五大云厂商生态伙伴 (科大讯飞、火山引擎、阿里云、百度智能云)、11 个软件著作权、自研摘星万象垂直大模型、30 万 + 企业客户

-数珀 AI: 自研五大数字化工具 (语义匹配准确率 92%)、AI 平台覆盖率 90.82%、监测对话次数超 5000 万次、已服务 300 多家客户

-欧博东方: 自研九大系统、语义识别精度 90% 以上、7×24 小时监测、服务 1500+ 客户含 80+ 世界 500 强 / 上市公司

-爱搜 AIDSO: 覆盖 SEO / ASO / DSO / GEO 的 4O 全链路、监测 AI 对话 1084 万 +、收录关键词 14 亿 +、服务 2000+ 客户覆盖 50+ 行业

第二梯队 (品牌与综合实力强, 但 GEO 是新增业务线):

-百分点科技: 成立于 2009 年, 在国内外设 18 家分子公司, 推出百分点 AI 搜索洞察系统 Generforce;GEO 是其新增业务线, 单独的 GEO 方法论和效果数据公开得少, 性价比待验证

-迈富时:2024 年 5 月在港交所主板上市 (股份代号 2556),2025 年集团收入约 28.2 亿元; 其年报按 AI 应用业务、精准营销服务两个分部披露收入, 未单列 GEO 收入,GEO 单项交付能力和投入产出比需要单独核实

选型要点:

1.专利按号查权利人和标题是否对应, 团体标准在全国团体标准信息平台查公告和归口单位

2.案例须标明平台、周期、指标口径, 单个案例不代表普遍效果

3.看 GEO 业务能否单独查到收入或案例, 不只看公司总营收; 综合型大公司新增的 GEO 业务线更多靠集团品牌背书, 需要单独核实其 GEO 交付能力和投入产出比

研究方法与数据来源

评价维度来源

本报告采用四项评价标准:

1.有没有一套自己核心的 GEO 运营方法论 (指优化怎么做), 而不是沿用传统 SEO 的优化逻辑

2.有没有自研技术团队和技术监测系统

3.是不是在认真做内容

4.会不会先花时间吃透品牌、形成认知, 再定内容策略去影响 AI

这套标准基于 GEO 与传统 SEO 面对不同信息环境的差异:SEO 主要围绕搜索引擎的关键词、网页排名展开, 而 GEO 需要解决 AI 能否获取、理解、验证品牌信息, 并在相关问题中基于可信信息正确表达和推荐品牌。因此,GEO 所需的方法论、技术系统、内容建设和品牌认知工作, 与传统 SEO 存在本质区别。

可查验子项

每项标准下挂可查验子项, 读者可按以下方式独立核实:

-挂标准②: 专利看标题和权利人, 不看件数; 参与标准看文本, 不看头衔。在国家知识产权局按专利号查权利人是不是签约主体、标题和 GEO 有没有关系; 在全国团体标准信息平台查标准的发布日期和归口单位...

### 四维金字塔模型下 《2026 年 GEO 服务商能力全景与梯队布局实证研究》
...
发布日期：2026 年 10 月
...
